# synth: invented tenders on mock sites, with a score

A stand-in for the private dataset: every seed is one invented tender on four local websites with their own look,
and an expected answer worked out without the agent's code. Nothing here is part of the package (`agent/`), nothing
here is copied from the challenge websites, and nothing learned from one seed may go into `agent/` as site knowledge:
a failing seed shows what is too specific in the agent; the fix has to be general.

## Use

From the repo root (`uv run --project agent` gives the agent's Python and Playwright):

```sh
dev/run-synth.sh v3 "what changed" platform-hazards 0-4      # agent runs, scored; needs `atira models proxy`
uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py check --seeds 300 --dataset mixed   # oracle vs calc.py, form round trip
uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py show --seed 7 --dataset one-trap    # features, look, expected answer
uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py serve --seed 7                      # browse the four sites yourself
uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py report [--version v3] [--dataset mixed]
python3 -m unittest discover -s dev/synth/tests                                    # the sites' hazards, about 1 s
```

Runs go to `experiments/synth-runs.jsonl` (gitignored) and show up in `docs/experiments.md` through
`python3 dev/track.py report`. `GENERATION` in `scenario.py` is recorded with every run: a seed means another
scenario in another generation, so compare runs of one generation only.

## What a run measures

| | How | How far to trust it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quality | `oracle.score`: the rule-29 weights on the signed bid, positions matched by number | The number to steer by. The two "when present" 5-point checks are our reading, not confirmed by the platform |
| Time | Start of the agent to the signed bid | Local sites answer faster than the sandbox: compare versions, do not predict |
| Cost | The trace's tokens at the simulated prices in `prices.json` (read from the platform's start page, dated) | Same: for comparing versions. Own-key models have no price here and record none |
| Cost x time | With the platform's floors ($0.01, 1 s) | The tie-breaker at equal quality |

## Datasets

`run.py show --help` lists them; `scenario.DATASETS` says what each one is. `mixed` draws everything, `one-trap`
puts exactly one rule's trap on a plain tender (the seed picks it from `scenario.TRAPS`), the others fix one oddity.
Added in generation 4:

| Dataset | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `platform-hazards` | Plain bid rules on sites with every platform hazard on |
| `replaced-assignments` | Packaging, commitment, pool and bonus keys assigned, replaced, and assigned again for a later date (rule 21) |
| `split-commitments` | Two positions on one material with different commitments, one a piece over its ceiling (rule 24) |
| `no-candidate` | no_bid cases where no material with the required attributes exists in any status (rules 3, 8) |
| `spoofed-approvals` | A newer approval under the director's name from another address (rules 5, 21) |
| `cent-rules` | Each of the five setup-pool cent rules in turn (rule 25) |

Also new in `mixed`: stock that covers each position of a material but not their sum (rule 15), amendments scoped to
any revision that does not govern (rule 14), reserve keys no requirement names (rule 20).

## Platform hazards

`sites.PLATFORM`, each drawn on or off per seed (all on where a dataset sets `platform: all`). They are the kinds
of obstacle real portals put in the way, written here from scratch with invented labels:

| Hazard | What the agent meets |
| --- | --- |
| `frames` | The specification's requirements and a mail's text sit in a frame with its own paging |
| `cascade` | In the bid form the catalogue group is chosen first and decides which materials the next list offers |
| `interest` | A tender's documents, questions and bid form open only after taking part is declared |
| `decoys` | Hidden instructions on every page, an overlay that comes back with its controls reordered, a button that discards the step's entries |
| `expiry` | Sessions end after one to three minutes on every site; a saved draft stays |
| `searchhelp` | The ERP search runs inside one catalogue group; a value help lists the groups |
| `routes` | The sites' addresses use this seed's own words |
| `fieldnames` | The bid form's fields carry this seed's own names |

`run.py check` enters every expected bid through whatever hazards a seed has and must score 100, so a hazard makes
a page harder to operate, never ambiguous. `report` shows mean quality with and without each hazard.

## Limits

- The sites are server-rendered German HTML. There are no file downloads, no archives and no canvas-drawn labels.
- Which site holds what varies only for the bidder Q&A. Stock, prices, set sizes and reserves stay where they are.
- Rule 9 has no trap of its own: the rules give no case where leaving a position out is the right answer, so the
  expected bid always holds every position.
- One setup pool and one bonus plan per tender, as rules 25 and 26 state them.
- The no_bid split (75/5/5/15) and the bid weights follow `scoring.md`; anything the platform checks beyond that is
  unknown.

content.text:
Yes, and one of your branches is a much better starting point than the starter pack — but it needs an adapter before the platform can host it. The two branches are very different cases.

**`private-data-simulation` (`dev/synth/`): use this one**

This is already what an eval is meant to be: invented tenders on four mock sites with a computed expected answer.

- **Coverage:** it covers the full 29-rule set with traps (spoofed approvals, replaced key assignments, all five pool cent rules, `no_bid` with no candidate), which the starter's six rules don't.
- **Hostile UI:** frames, dependent form choices, overlays, short sessions, and per-seed routes and field names.
- **Varied look:** site names, navigation, paging and date notation change per seed.
- **It already found real bugs:** the first two runs on it scored 24 and 0, both from bid-form failures that public-1 never shows.

**`sim-portals` (`sim/`): don't deploy this one**

It replays recorded pages of the real public-1 sites. As an eval it would only re-test public-1, which you already score 100 on, and it would mean uploading content copied from the challenge sites. It stays useful as a local offline mirror.

**What the adapter has to do**

`dev/synth` runs locally with its own login and keeps the signed bid in memory. A platform eval needs:

1. **A bundle per scenario:** `atira-eval.json`, a `BRIEF.md` and an `expected.json` generated from one seed. One eval is one world, and the limit is 10 evals per team, so you pick up to 10 seeds.
2. **Platform login and answer:** sign agents in through the platform's verify endpoint and hand the signed bid to its answer endpoint, instead of the local equivalents.
3. **Per-run state:** one server instance serves every run, so drafts and TANs must be keyed by run id.
4. **Platform ports and URLs:** listen on the ports the platform assigns and use its public URLs for links between sites.

One unknown: the synth sites are Python, and the eval docs only show Node apps. I haven't checked whether the eval machines have Python; if not, the build step would need to fetch it.

One difference to expect: the eval scorer only scores material, quantity, unit price and lead time per position. Base price, surcharge, packaging and rebate are accepted but not scored, so platform eval scores will be coarser than `dev/synth`'s own scoring.

That branch is checked out in a separate worktree (`error404ai_ehl_finals-pds`), which looks like someone's active work. Should I build the adapter there, or on a new branch off it?
what do you mean by 10 evals per team ?

It's a platform limit: your team can have at most 10 evals deployed on the platform at one time (the docs say "10 evals a team", unless the organizers change it).

One eval is one fixed world: one set of sites, one brief and one `expected.json`. So one eval tests the agent on exactly one scenario.

That matters for `dev/synth` because it works differently. Locally it generates a fresh tender from any seed number, so you can run hundreds of scenarios. On the platform, each seed you want to test has to be deployed as its own eval, so you get at most 10 scenarios there at a time.

What the limit does not restrict:

- **Runs:** you can run agents on each eval as often as you like, within 12 eval runs per hour.
- **Versions:** redeploying an eval pushes a new version of the same eval, which doesn't use up another slot.
- **Swapping:** `atira eval rm` deletes one and frees its slot.
- **Other teams' public evals:** running on those doesn't count against your 10.

So the practical approach is to keep using `dev/synth` locally for breadth, and pick the 10 most revealing seeds (for example one per trap type, plus a `no_bid` case) to deploy as platform evals.

The "adapter" is the glue code between your `dev/synth` sites and the platform's eval hosting. Nothing like it exists yet; it's the piece I was proposing to write. `dev/synth` was built to run on your laptop, and it differs from what the platform expects in five places:

| What | `dev/synth` today | What a platform eval needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Login** | Each site invents its own username and password at start-up and checks them itself | The platform issues a login per run; the site must check it by calling the platform's verify endpoint |
| **Answer** | The signed bid is stored in memory and scored locally by `oracle.py` | The site must send the signed bid to the platform's answer endpoint, which scores it and ends the run |
| **State** | One server process serves one run: one signed bid, one set of drafts and sessions | One server serves every run of that eval, so drafts, TANs and the signed bid must be kept separately per run id |
| **Network** | Listens on `127.0.0.1` with random ports; links between sites use those local addresses | Must listen on the ports the platform assigns and use the public URLs it provides |
| **Packaging** | A seed number generates the world on the fly; the brief and expected answer live in Python | A folder with `atira-eval.json`, a `BRIEF.md` and an `expected.json` written out for one chosen seed |

The pieces to build:

1. **A Python version of the login and answer calls.** The starter kit's `atira-kit.js` does this for Node; the synth sites are Python, so the same two HTTP calls need rewriting.
2. **Per-run state in `sites.py`.** `App.signed`, the tender site's saved drafts and the session tables become keyed by run id.
3. **An export command** that takes a seed and dataset and writes the bundle folder: manifest, brief, expected answer and the site code.

Some of the groundwork is there: `run.py` already has an `export` function that dumps a scenario with its brief and expected answer, and the sites use only the Python standard library, so there are no dependencies to install.

The open risk is unchanged: the eval docs say nothing about which runtimes the eval machines have, and every example is Node. If Python isn't there, the fallback is a build step that fetches it, since builds can reach package registries. That would be the first thing to test with a trivial deploy before writing the rest.

#!/bin/sh
# Run the agent locally against synthetic scenarios (dev/synth: invented tenders on four mock sites) and record
# each run's quality, time and cost in experiments/synth-runs.jsonl (gitignored).
# Usage, from anywhere: dev/run-synth.sh <version> ["note"] [dataset] [seeds]
#   dataset: one of `python3 dev/synth/run.py show --help` (default mixed); seeds: e.g. 0-4 or 3,7,12 (default 0-2)
# Needs `atira models proxy` running in another terminal (or QWEN_BASE_URL/QWEN_API_KEY set). HEADLESS=0 shows the
# browser. The sites of one seed are the same on every run; nothing may be tuned to a single seed.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/run-synth.sh <version> [note] [dataset] [seeds]}
note=${2:-}
dataset=${3:-mixed}
seeds=${4:-0-2}
(cd agent && uv sync -q)
uv run --no-sync --project agent python dev/synth/run.py agent --seeds "$seeds" --dataset "$dataset" \
  --version "$version" --note "$note" || exit $?
uv run --no-sync --project agent python dev/synth/run.py report --version "$version" --dataset "$dataset"
python3 dev/track.py report

# Prepare a tender response

You work in sales engineering for Beispiel Hydraulik GmbH, a German hydraulics manufacturer. Prepare one net EUR bid for Wasserverband Musterstadt: Hydraulikzylinder für das Schleusentor Süd (VG-2026-0815). The scenario date is 2026-10-08T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2026-10-30T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`, bidder mailbox vertrieb@beispiel-hydraulik.example). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.

2	Synthetic scenarios for the agent: generate, check, browse, and run the agent against them with a score.
3	
4	Each seed is one invented tender on four local websites with their own look (see scenario.py and sites.py). The
5	expected answer comes from oracle.py, so a run gets the same breakdown a sandbox test run shows, for data and
6	layouts the agent has never seen. Nothing here is part of the package, and nothing here may flow back into
7	`agent/` as site knowledge: use a failing seed to find what is too specific in the agent, then fix that in general.
8	
9	From the repo root (`uv run --project agent` gives the agent's Python and Playwright):
10	    uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py check --seeds 300      # oracle vs agent/calc.py, form round trip
11	    uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py show --seed 7          # features, look and expected answer
12	    uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py serve --seed 7         # browse the four sites yourself
13	    uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py agent --seeds 7,8,9    # needs `atira models proxy` running
14	    uv run --project agent python dev/synth/run.py export --seeds 0-19    # plain JSON for another environment
15	Results of `agent` go to experiments/synth-runs.jsonl (gitignored); `report` summarises them by dataset, feature
16	and look. Each run records what the platform ranks by: quality (the rule-29 scorer), time (start of the agent to
17	the signed bid) and cost (the trace's tokens at the simulated prices in prices.json), and cost x time with the
18	platform's floors. Time and cost are measured on this machine against local sites: they compare two versions of
19	the agent with each other, they do not predict a scored run's figures.

111	def judge(app: sites.App, expected: dict) -> dict:
112	    """The score of the signed bid, with the form's own traps counted (an alternative offer is not a bid)."""
113	    signed = app.signed
114	    answer = signed and dict(signed["answer"])
115	    if answer and signed["meta"]["offer_type"] == "neben":
116	        answer["decision"] = "alternative_offer"
117	    result = oracle.score(app.world, expected, answer)
118	    if signed:
119	        w = app.world
120	        meta = signed["meta"]
121	        result["form"] = {"own_terms_declared": meta["own_terms"], "omitted": meta["omitted"],
122	                          "extra_rows": meta["extra_rows"], "tan_requests": meta["tan_requests"],
123	                          "discards": meta["discards"],
124	                          "company_ok": meta["company"] == w.company and meta["vat"] == w.vat,
125	                          "contact_ok": meta["email"].casefold() == w.mailbox.casefold()}
126	        result["seconds"] = meta["seconds"]
127	    return result

133	class Client:
134	    """Fills the bid form over plain HTTP with a given answer: proves a scenario's form and scoring work.
135	    It knows the form's field names, so it says nothing about the agent."""
136	
137	    def __init__(self, site: sites.Site, entry: str = ""):
138	        self.site, self.entry = site, entry  # entry: the address of a tender's entry step, when it has one
139	        self.opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.HTTPCookieProcessor(CookieJar()))
140	
141	    def call(self, path: str, form: dict | None = None) -> str:
142	        """A page by the address and field names of the sites' code, whatever this seed's sites call them. A
143	        temporary error is asked again; a session that ended is signed in again."""
144	        data = urlencode(form).encode() if form is not None else None
145	        for _ in range(4):
146	            with self.opener.open(self.site.url + self.site.skin.out_path(path), data, timeout=10) as response:
147	                text = response.read().decode()
148	            if 'type="password"' in text and path != "/login":
149	                self.sign_in()
150	            elif "vorübergehend nicht verfügbar" not in text:
151	                return text
152	        return text
153	
154	    def sign_in(self) -> None:
155	        self.call("/login", {"username": self.site.user, "password": self.site.password, "next": "/"})
156	        self.call("/consent", {"wahl": "notwendig", "next": "/"})
157	        if self.entry:
158	            self.call(self.entry, {"bestaetigt": "1", "next": "/"})

161	def enter(app: sites.App, answer: dict) -> None:
162	    w = app.world
163	    base = f"/a/{w.tender.tid}/angebot"
164	    client = Client(app.sites["tender"], f"/a/{w.tender.tid}/teilnahme" if "interest" in app.skin.platform else "")
165	    client.sign_in()
166	    name = app.skin.field
167	    by_number = {p["position"]: p for p in answer["positions"]}
168	    values = {"firma": w.company, "ustid": w.vat, "email": w.mailbox, "anerkannt": "1",
169	              "art": "verzicht" if answer["decision"] == "no_bid" else "haupt",
170	              "rabatt": scenario.plain(answer["discount_percent"]), "summe": scenario.de(answer["total_net"])}
171	    for i, p in enumerate(w.tender.positions):
172	        row = by_number.get(p.number)
173	        if row is None:
174	            values[f"p{i}_auslassen"] = "1"
175	            continue
176	        values.update({f"p{i}_material": row["material_number"], f"p{i}_menge": str(row["quantity"]),
177	                       f"p{i}_preis": scenario.de(row["unit_price"]), f"p{i}_lieferzeit": str(row["lead_time_weeks"]),
178	                       f"p{i}_basis": scenario.de(row["base_unit_price"]),
179	                       f"p{i}_zuschlag": scenario.de(row["surcharge_per_unit"]),
180	                       f"p{i}_verpackung": scenario.de(row["packaging_per_unit"]),
181	                       f"p{i}_bonus": scenario.de(row["rebate_total"])})
182	    values = {name(k): v for k, v in values.items()}
183	    step = 1
184	    while True:
185	        page = client.call(f"{base}?schritt={step}")
186	        names = set(re.findall(r'name="([^"]+)"', page)) - {"aktion", "schritt"}
187	        form = {n: values[n] for n in names if n in values}
188	        page = client.call(base, {**form, "schritt": str(step), "aktion": "weiter"})
189	        if "TAN anfordern" in page or "kann noch nicht" in page:
190	            break
191	        step += 1
192	    client.call(base + "/pruefen", {"aktion": "tan"})
193	    client.call(base + "/pruefen", {"aktion": "abgeben", "tan": app.tans[w.tender.tid]["tan"]})

196	def cmd_check(args) -> int:
197	    bad, decisions = 0, collections.Counter()
198	    for seed in range(args.first, args.first + args.seeds):
199	        world = scenario.generate(seed, args.dataset)
200	        expected = oracle.solve(world)
201	        decisions[expected["decision"]] += 1
202	        problems = []
203	        if oracle.via_calc(world) != expected:
204	            problems.append("agent/calc.py disagrees with the oracle")
205	        if seed < args.first + args.forms:
206	            app = sites.App(world)
207	            servers = sites.start(app)
208	            try:
209	                enter(app, expected)
210	                result = judge(app, expected)
211	                if result["quality"] != 100 or not result["eligible"]:
212	                    problems.append(f"form round trip scored {result['quality']}: {result['wrong'][:3]}")
213	            except Exception as error:
214	                problems.append(f"form round trip failed: {error!r}")
215	            finally:
216	                for server in servers:
217	                    server.shutdown()
218	        if problems:
219	            bad += 1
220	            print(f"seed {seed}: {'; '.join(problems)}")
221	    print(f"{args.seeds} scenarios ({dict(decisions)}), {min(args.forms, args.seeds)} form round trips: "
222	          f"{bad or 'no'} problem(s)")
223	    return 1 if bad else 0

340	def usage(traces: Path, model: str) -> dict:
341	    """The tokens a run's trace reports and their cost at the simulated prices (None for a model without one).
342	    Every event that carries token counts is summed: finished workers, stopped ones and single extraction calls."""
343	    tokens = {"input_tokens": 0, "cached_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}
344	    for path in traces.glob("run-*.jsonl"):
345	        for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
346	            try:
347	                event = json.loads(line)
348	            except ValueError:
349	                continue  # a run killed mid-write leaves a partial last line
350	            for key in tokens:
351	                tokens[key] += event.get(key) or 0
352	    price = next((p for name, p in PRICES.items() if name in model.casefold()), None)
353	    cost = None
354	    if price:
355	        fresh = max(0, tokens["input_tokens"] - tokens["cached_tokens"])
356	        cost = round((fresh * price["input"] + tokens["cached_tokens"] * price["cached_input"]
357	                      + tokens["output_tokens"] * price["output"]) / 1_000_000, 4)
358	    return {**tokens, "model": model, "cost_usd": cost}

364	    app = sites.App(world)
365	    sites.start(app)
366	    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN", "CHALLENGE_API_URL")}
367	    traces = ROOT / "agent" / "traces" / f"synth-{seed}-{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}"
368	    traces.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
369	    env.update(CHALLENGE_SCOUTING=json.dumps(build_run(app, args.minutes * 60)), TRACE_DIR=str(traces),
370	               HEADLESS=env.get("HEADLESS", "1"), NO_PROXY="127.0.0.1,localhost", no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost")
371	    env.setdefault("QWEN_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1")
372	    env.setdefault("QWEN_API_KEY", "local")
373	    started = time.time()
374	    with (traces / "agent.log").open("w") as log:
375	        try:
376	            code = subprocess.run(["uv", "run", "--no-sync", "python", "agent.py"], cwd=ROOT / "agent", env=env,
377	                                  stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=args.minutes * 60 + 120).returncode
378	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

380	    result = judge(app, expected)
381	    used = usage(traces, env.get("LLM_MODEL") or env.get("AGENT_MODEL") or "qwen")
382	    seconds = result.get("seconds") or round(time.time() - started, 1)  # no signed bid: the whole run counts
383	    used["cost_x_time"] = None if used["cost_usd"] is None else round(max(used["cost_usd"], 0.01) * max(seconds, 1), 2)
384	    commit = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

418	    if not RESULTS.exists():
419	        print("No synthetic runs recorded yet.")

448	def summary(runs: list[dict]) -> str:
449	    """Quality, time and cost of a set of runs in one line, as the platform ranks: quality, then cost x time."""
450	    def mean(key: str) -> str:
451	        values = [r[key] for r in runs if r.get(key) is not None]
452	        return f"{sum(values) / len(values):.4g}" if values else "-"
453	
454	    return (f"{len(runs)} runs, mean quality {sum(r['quality'] for r in runs) / max(1, len(runs)):.1f}, "
455	            f"{sum(r['quality'] == 100 for r in runs)} at 100, {sum(not r['eligible'] for r in runs)} not eligible, "
456	            f"mean {mean('seconds')} s, ${mean('cost_usd')}, cost x time {mean('cost_x_time')}")

""" One synthetic scenario as a platform eval (docs/evals.md): the four mock sites on the platform's ports, signing in with the logins the platform hands each run, and the signed bid handed to the platform, which scores it. `run.py bundle` copies this file into an eval folder as `server.py`, beside scenario.py, sites.py, oracle.py, `eval.json` (seed and dataset), BRIEF.md and expected.json. The platform starts it with PORT_ per site, ATIRA_API_URL and ATIRA_EVAL_TOKEN; `atira eval dev` does the same here with a local stand-in. One process serves every run of the eval, so each run (and each preview) gets its own `sites.App`: its own drafts, sessions, TANs and scenario clock, started at its first sign-in. """
The synthetic sites as a platform eval (evalapp.py), against a stand-in for the platform's two endpoints: the
platform's logins sign in, each run has its own state, and the signed bid reaches the platform as the expected
answer. No browser and no model. From the repo root: python3 -m unittest discover -s dev/synth/tests
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
import urllib.error
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

import evalapp  # noqa: E402
import run  # noqa: E402

LOGINS = {"u_one": ("run_id", "run_1"), "u_two": ("run_id", "run_2"), "p_look": ("preview_id", "prev_1")}


class Platform(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """The platform's verify and answer endpoints; what it was sent is kept on the server."""

    def log_message(self, *args) -> None:
        pass

    def do_POST(self) -> None:
        payload = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers["Content-Length"])))
        state = self.server.state  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        status, body = 401, {}
        if self.headers.get("Authorization") != "Bearer secret":
            pass
        elif self.path == "/v1/eval-worlds/verify":
            known = LOGINS.get(payload["username"])
            if known and payload["password"] == "pw" and payload["username"] not in state["ended"]:
                status, body = 200, {known[0]: known[1], "expires_at": int((time.time() + 1200) * 1000)}
        elif self.path == "/v1/eval-worlds/answer":
            state["answers"].append(payload)
            if state["issues"]:
                status, body = 400, {"issues": state["issues"]}
            elif "run_id" in payload:
                status, body = 202, {"accepted": True}
            else:
                status, body = 200, {"accepted": True, "score": {"quality": 100, "eligible": True}}
        raw = json.dumps(body).encode()
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(raw)


class EvalApp(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        folder = run.bundle(3, "platform-hazards", Path(self.folder.name))
        self.platform = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Platform)
        self.platform.state = {"answers": [], "issues": [], "ended": set()}
        threading.Thread(target=self.platform.serve_forever, args=(0.02,), daemon=True).start()
        self.eval = evalapp.Eval(folder)
        names = [site["name"] for site in self.eval.manifest["sites"]]
        env = {"ATIRA_API_URL": f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.platform.server_address[1]}", "ATIRA_EVAL_TOKEN": "secret",
               **{f"PORT_{evalapp.variable(name)}": "0" for name in names}}
        patch = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, env)
        patch.start()
        self.addCleanup(patch.stop)
        self.servers = evalapp.start(self.eval, "127.0.0.1")
        self.urls = {server.name: f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}" for server in self.servers}

    def tearDown(self):
        for server in [*self.servers, self.platform]:
            server.shutdown()
            server.server_close()
        self.folder.cleanup()

    def run_app(self, key: str, username: str):
        """A run's own sites, addressed and signed in the way the platform's login does it."""
        app = self.eval.app(key, time.time() + 1200)
        for site in app.sites.values():
            site.url, site.user, site.password = self.urls[site.sid], username, "pw"
        return app

    def test_the_bundle_matches_what_is_generated_here(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.eval.problems(), [])
        self.eval.expected["total_net"] += 1
        self.assertEqual(len(self.eval.problems()), 1)

    def test_a_signed_bid_reaches_the_platform_as_the_expected_answer(self):
        run.enter(self.run_app("run:run_1", "u_one"), self.eval.expected)
        self.assertEqual(self.platform.state["answers"], [{"run_id": "run_1", "bid": self.eval.expected}])

    def test_each_run_has_its_own_bid(self):
        run.enter(self.run_app("run:run_1", "u_one"), self.eval.expected)

Not ready yet — the adapter works locally, but the first live run exposed a bug and I'm waiting on the run that confirms the fix.

- **Built:** `dev/synth/evalapp.py` serves any synth scenario as a platform eval, and `run.py bundle` writes the eval folder. It's on a new branch `synth-evals` in a separate worktree (`error404ai_ehl_finals-evals`), uncommitted.
- **Verified locally:** 22 tests pass, and entering the expected bid through `atira eval dev` scored 100 on the platform's stand-in.
- **Deployed:** one private eval, `err404-synth-hazards-0` (the `platform-hazards` dataset, seed 0). The platform's build generates the same scenario as the bundled expected answer.
- **Bug found live:** in the first run the agent looped on the login pages of the mail and spec sites from about 2:20 onward. My best explanation is that the adapter asked the platform to verify each tab's login separately and got rate-limited; I couldn't see the eval server's own log to confirm that.
- **Fix:** login checks are now shared per run and site (one platform call per 10 s), and a login the platform already accepted stays valid while it is busy. Redeployed; a second run of the current submission is in progress.

I'll report the result when that run finishes. Two things I noticed along the way:

- Your team already has three evals from teammates (`err404-traps`, `err404-nobid`, `err404-layout`), and the current submission scored 36.3, 0 and 5 on them. That's a strong sign the 100 on public-1 doesn't carry over.
- You're now using 5 of 10 eval slots, and I've used 2 of the shared 12 eval runs per hour.

"""
Quick decisions with Cloudflare Clef, the hosted decision model, beside Qwen.

Clef answers fixed-form questions about a state in about a second: `choice` picks one of our options, `noul` gives the
probability of yes. Off unless AGENT_CLEF=1 (or USE_CLEF=1), so runs with and without it compare side by side; ship
it on only with "clef" in agent.json "models". Every helper returns None when Clef fails, and the caller goes on
without it.

Measured on hand-labelled page views (dev/clef_eval/RESULTS.md): Clef loses to Qwen without thinking at picking a
link and at judging whether a record is the right one (ordering, look-alike references, numbers), but it is exact and
fast at "is this an error, empty, locked or decoy page after my action", where Qwen without thinking slips. So the
only agent use is that check: the `page_check` tool, and `outcome_hint` for a hook after actions.
"""
import asyncio
import os
import re
import time

import httpx2 as httpx
from pydantic_ai import RunContext

TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("CLEF_TIMEOUT", "20"))
MAX_STATE = 12000  # characters of page text sent; Clef reads text far shorter than Qwen's context
_limit = asyncio.Semaphore(int(os.environ.get("CLEF_CONCURRENCY", "12")))  # team limit is 16 at once
USAGE = {"calls": 0, "input_tokens": 0, "seconds": 0.0}  # this process's Clef use, for the trace and cost
ELEMENT = re.compile(r"\[(e\d+) (link|button|summary|tab|menuitem)\b([^\]]*)\]")


def enabled() -> bool:
    on = os.environ.get("AGENT_CLEF", os.environ.get("USE_CLEF", "0")) == "1"
    return on and bool(os.environ.get("CLEF_BASE_URL"))


async def decide(state, questions: dict, images: list[str] | None = None, retries: int = 2) -> dict | None:
    """One /v1/decide call: the raw answers by question key, or None after `retries` failed attempts."""
    if not os.environ.get("CLEF_BASE_URL"):
        return None
    body = {"state": state, "questions": questions}
    if images:
        body["images"] = images[:4]
    url = os.environ["CLEF_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/decide"
    headers = {"User-Agent": "error404ai-rfq-agent"}
    if os.environ.get("CLEF_API_KEY"):
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {os.environ['CLEF_API_KEY']}"
    for attempt in range(retries + 1):
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            async with _limit, httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=TIMEOUT) as client:
                response = await client.post(url, json=body, headers=headers)
            response.raise_for_status()
            data = response.json()
            tokens = data.get("usage", {}).get("input_tokens", 0)
            USAGE["calls"] += 1
            USAGE["input_tokens"] += tokens
            USAGE["seconds"] += time.monotonic() - started
            print(f"[clef] {response.status_code} {time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s {tokens} tokens", flush=True)
            return data["answers"]
        except Exception as error:
            print(f"[clef] failed ({type(error).__name__}: {str(error)[:120]})", flush=True)
            if attempt < retries:
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5 * (attempt + 1))
    return None


def options_from_view(view: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The links and buttons of a page view by ref, each with the words of its row, for a `choice` question."""
    options: dict[str, str] = {}
    lines = view.splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        matches = list(ELEMENT.finditer(line))
        if not matches:
            continue
        row = ELEMENT.sub(lambda m: m.group(3).strip(), line).strip()
        if len(ELEMENT.sub("", line).strip(" |-")) < 3 and i:  # a row of bare controls: name what precedes it
            row = f"{lines[i - 1].strip()[:120]} / {row}"
        for m in matches:
            options[m.group(1)] = f"{m.group(2)} {m.group(3).strip()}  (row: {row[:240]})"
    return options


async def choose(view: str, goal: str, options: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> tuple[str, float] | None:
    """Which option (by key) best serves `goal` on this view, and Clef's probability for it."""
    options = options or options_from_view(view)
    if not options:
        return None
    answers = await decide({"goal": goal, "page": view[:MAX_STATE]},
                           {"pick": {"type": "choice", "instructions": f"Which element should be used next to reach "
                                     f"the goal: {goal}", "criteria": options}})
    if not answers:
        return None
    pick = answers["pick"]
    return pick["choice"], pick.get("probabilities", {}).get(pick["choice"], pick.get("confidence", 0.0))


async def yes(state, question: str) -> float | None:
    """Clef's probability that the answer to a yes/no question about `state` is yes."""
    answers = await decide(state, {"q": {"type": "noul", "instructions": question}})
    return None if answers is None else answers["q"]["noul"]


async def yes_each(state, questions: list[str]) -> list[float] | None:
    """Several yes/no questions about one state in one call (e.g. one per list row), in order."""
    answers = await decide(state, {f"q{i}": {"type": "noul", "instructions": q} for i, q in enumerate(questions)})
    return None if answers is None else [answers[f"q{i}"]["noul"] for i in range(len(questions))]


OUTCOME_QUESTION = ("Is this page an error, an empty result, a locked or expired state, a dead end or a decoy, rather "
                    "than real content that moves the task on? Last action: {action}")


async def dead_end(view: str, action: str) -> float | None:
    """Clef's probability that `view`, seen after `action`, is an error, empty, locked or decoy page."""
    return await yes({"last_action": action, "page": view[:MAX_STATE]}, OUTCOME_QUESTION.format(action=action))


async def outcome_hint(view: str, action: str) -> str:
    """A line to put above a view when Clef finds it a dead end after `action` (threshold 0.5), else ""."""
    p = await dead_end(view, action) if enabled() else None
    return "" if p is None or p < 0.5 else (f"Check: this looks like an error, empty, locked or decoy page after "
                                             f"{action} (p={p:.2f}); go back or try another way.")


async def page_check(ctx: RunContext, last_action: str) -> str:
    """Ask a fast second opinion whether the current page is an error, empty, locked or decoy page after an action.

    Use it when unsure whether your last action worked, before relying on the page. `last_action` says what you
    did and expected, e.g. "searched the archive for the tender reference".
    """
    session = ctx.deps.session
    p = await dead_end(session.view, last_action)
    session.trace.event(session.name, "clef", check="outcome", action=last_action[:120], p_error=p)
    if p is None:
        return "No second opinion available; judge the page yourself."
    if p >= 0.5:
        return f"Likely an error, empty, locked or decoy page (p={p:.2f}): go back or try another way."
    return f"Likely real content (p_error={p:.2f}); the action seems to have worked."


def tools() -> tuple:
    """Extra worker tools when Clef is on; pass to run_worker(tools=...)."""
    return (page_check,) if enabled() else ()

# Who made each model call. Agent.run (patched below) sets LABEL to the agent function that called it: the nearest
# frame in this package outside llm.py and worker.py, or for run_worker the worker kind it set. pydantic-ai makes the
# request in tasks of its own, where the caller's frames are gone but the context variable carries over. USAGE sums
# each label's calls, so the run summary shows where calls, tokens and seconds went (the platform's call list has
# no caller).
LABEL: contextvars.ContextVar[str] = contextvars.ContextVar("llm_label", default="")
USAGE: dict[str, list[float]] = {}  # label -> [calls, input, cached, output, seconds, thinking-on calls]
_PACKAGE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
_NOT_CALLERS = ("llm.py", "worker.py")


def caller() -> str:
    """The agent function the current Agent.run serves (see LABEL)."""
    frame = sys._getframe(1)
    while frame is not None:
        path = frame.f_code.co_filename
        name = os.path.basename(path)
        if name == "worker.py" and LABEL.get():
            return LABEL.get()
        if path.endswith(".py") and os.path.dirname(path) == _PACKAGE and name not in _NOT_CALLERS:
            return f"{name[:-3]}.{frame.f_code.co_name}"
        frame = frame.f_back
    return LABEL.get() or "other"


def _labelled(run):
    @functools.wraps(run)
    async def labelled_run(self, *args, **kwargs):
        token = LABEL.set(caller())
        try:
            return await run(self, *args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            LABEL.reset(token)
    return labelled_run


if not getattr(AbstractAgent.run, "_labelled", False):
    AbstractAgent.run = _labelled(AbstractAgent.run)  # type: ignore[method-assign]
    AbstractAgent.run._labelled = True  # type: ignore[attr-defined]


def record(label: str, response: ModelResponse, seconds: float, thinking: bool) -> None:
    usage = response.usage
    row = USAGE.setdefault(label, [0, 0, 0, 0, 0.0, 0])
    for i, value in enumerate((1, usage.input_tokens, usage.cache_read_tokens, usage.output_tokens, seconds,
                               int(thinking))):
        row[i] += value


def usage_table() -> str:
    """USAGE as lines, most input first, with each label's share of the simulated cost (Qwen's input, cached and
    output prices per token as the platform listed them; only the shares matter)."""
    def cost(row):
        return (row[1] - row[2]) * 0.15 + row[2] * 0.016 + row[3] * 0.47
    total = sum(cost(row) for row in USAGE.values()) or 1.0
    lines = ["calls  think  input  cached  output  seconds  cost%  caller"]
    for label, row in sorted(USAGE.items(), key=lambda item: -cost(item[1])):
        lines.append(f"{row[0]:5.0f} {row[5]:6.0f} {row[1]:6.0f} {row[2]:7.0f} {row[3]:7.0f} {row[4]:8.1f} "
                     f"{100 * cost(row) / total:5.1f}  {label}")
    if FALLBACKS:
        lines.append("hosted fallbacks: " + ", ".join(f"{label} {n}" for label, n in sorted(FALLBACKS.items())))
    return "\n".join(lines)

content.text:
Zero cache writes is expected, and caching is not what's driving the cost; the step count is.

**Why writes show 0**
The hosted Qwen caches prompt prefixes automatically. It never bills or reports a separate "write", so the platform only shows reads. Explicit cache writes exist only on the Anthropic backend, which this run didn't use.

**Where the time and tokens go**
The one finished agent run on your portal (the current submission, `run_9d9529b549e4660e`) took 548 model calls, 11.6 minutes and $0.16, for quality 10. Its log shows why:

- **Mail research found almost nothing and kept retrying.** Workers for packaging, condition rules, setup pools and project bonus each hit their 20-request limit with nothing kept, and were then started again. That is roughly 6 of the 9 research minutes.
- **Each worker step resends the page.** A typical mail worker used about 65,000 input tokens over 16–18 requests, of which about 60 % came from the cache.
- **Uncached input is the expensive part.** At the prices in `docs/learned.md` (uncached $0.15/M, cached about $0.016/M, output $0.47/M), the 40 % uncached input costs several times more than all the cached input together.
- **No position was built.** Material selection came back empty for all four positions, so the bid went in with every position omitted.
- **Signing failed.** The model proxy answered 401 at the signing step, so the agent itself never submitted; the 10 points are the platform's score for the run regardless.

So on your portal the agent is spending most of its budget searching for records it doesn't find. That is a generalisation failure, and it costs both quality and money.

**What would actually cut cost**
1. Stop a mail search early when the first pass finds no candidates, instead of running to the limit and retrying.
2. Raise the cache share by keeping the prompt prefix stable between steps; trimming older page views changes the history and breaks the cached prefix.
3. Fewer, larger steps per worker.

The team's own note in `docs/learned.md` says the same: step count times view size is the lever, not caching.

My two comparison runs (plain `main`, and `main` with Clef) are still queued behind teammates' runs, so I don't have their numbers yet. That submission is also older than `main`, so `main` may behave differently. Do you want me to look into the early-stop for empty mail searches once those runs give a baseline?
when you do evals would you be testing against public data or private ones which we made ?>

Against the ones we made. An eval run uses only that eval's own sites, brief and expected answer; it never touches the organizers' public-1 sites or their private dataset.

The three kinds of run use three different datasets:

| Run | Command | Data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Test run | `atira test-run ./agent` | Organizers' public dataset (public-1) |
| Scored submission | `atira submit ./agent` | Organizers' public dataset (public-1) |
| Eval run | `atira eval run <eval> --package ...` | That eval's own world, written by a team |
| Final run | Started by the organizers | Organizers' private dataset, which nobody can see |

So the runs I started on `err404-synth-hazards-0` are tested against your synth portals, with the expected answer computed by `oracle.py`.

Two wording traps:

- The platform labels eval runs "eval run on the public dataset" in the run details. That label is misleading; the run log shows the agent working on the eval's own site addresses.
- "Private" for an eval only means visibility: private evals are usable by your team alone, public ones by every team. It has nothing to do with the organizers' private dataset.

Your evals are a stand-in for the organizers' private dataset, not a copy of it. A good score on them shows the agent copes with unfamiliar layouts and data, not that it will score the same in the final run.
on the evals page it says public dataset

That label is the platform's wording, and it's misleading for eval runs; the runs do go against your own portals. I saw the same text earlier in the run details: "eval run on the public dataset".

The run logs show what was actually used:

- **Tender reference:** the agent worked on tender `B25.9084` for "Albtal Fluidtechnik AG", which is the invented scenario from your synth generator (seed 0 of `platform-hazards`). It is not public-1's tender.
- **Site names:** the sites were `bietercockpit`, `partnernetz`, `fertigung-plus` and `groupmail`, the names your generator picked.
- **Site addresses:** every page was on an `evw-….kyora.run` address, which is the eval's own hosted world.
- **Scoring:** the bid I entered by hand through the preview scored 100 against the `expected.json` from your `oracle.py`.

My best guess is that the platform has only two dataset labels, "public" and "private", where "private" is reserved for the organizers' final run, so everything else is tagged "public". I haven't found that stated in the docs. It's worth mentioning to the organizers, since it will confuse other teams too.
just wanted to confirm if we were using our dataset
Yes, confirmed: every eval run on `err404-synth-hazards-0` uses your own dataset, the synth portals with the expected answer from `oracle.py`. The "public dataset" text is only the platform's label.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
One turn of the improve-and-measure loop on our own evals: name the agent as it stands, run it on the evals of
dev/train_rules.json, download every run's timed log, turn the scores into one reward by the rule in that file and
say whether this version beats the best so far.

    python3 dev/trainloop.py step "what changed"          # package agent/, run, wait, download, judge
    python3 dev/trainloop.py step "..." --evals a,b --repeats 2 --package submission
    python3 dev/trainloop.py adopt eve_... "note"         # judge an eval entry that already ran (no new runs)
    python3 dev/trainloop.py collect <version>            # finish a step whose wait was interrupted
    python3 dev/trainloop.py report                       # every version, best first

A version is named <prefix>-<date>-<time>-<zone> on the Central European clock (CET in winter, CEST in summer), and
its eval runs carry that name on the platform. Everything of a version is kept in experiments/train/<version>/
(gitignored): the package that ran, the rules, and per run its score and its log with the run's clock on every line.
experiments/train/ledger.jsonl holds one line per version.

The loop only measures. What to change between two steps is decided by reading the logs of the runs that lost
points, and the change has to be general: nothing seen on an eval's sites (values, labels, addresses) may go into
agent/. Each step costs evals x repeats of the team's eval runs (12 an hour, shared).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import zoneinfo
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
RULES = ROOT / "dev" / "train_rules.json"
TRAIN = ROOT / "experiments" / "train"
LEDGER = TRAIN / "ledger.jsonl"
WAITING = ("queued", "provisioning", "setup", "running", "starting", "pending")


def atira(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    done = subprocess.run(["atira", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    if check and done.returncode:
        raise SystemExit(f"atira {' '.join(args)} failed: {(done.stderr or done.stdout).strip()[:400]}")
    return done.stdout


def git(*args: str) -> str:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()


def rules() -> dict:
    return json.loads(RULES.read_text())


def new_version(prefix: str) -> str:
    now = datetime.datetime.now(zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin"))
    name = f"{prefix}-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M}-{now:%Z}"
    return name if not (TRAIN / name).exists() else f"{prefix}-{now:%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}-{now:%Z}"


def ledger() -> list[dict]:
    """One record per version: a later line of the same version replaces the earlier one."""
    if not LEDGER.exists():
        return []
    latest: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for line in LEDGER.read_text().splitlines():
        if line.strip():
            record = json.loads(line)
            latest[record["version"]] = record
    return list(latest.values())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the rule and the reward


def run_reward(run: dict, rule: dict) -> float:
    """A scored run's reward: its quality (the rule's `not_eligible` when it is not eligible) plus the rule's
    weight on cost x time, with the platform's floors ($0.01, 1 s)."""
    quality = run["quality"] if run["eligible"] else rule["not_eligible"]
    cost_x_time = max(run["cost_usd"], 0.01) * max(run["seconds"], 1.0)
    return rule["quality"] * quality + rule["cost_x_time"] * cost_x_time


def judge(record: dict, earlier: list[dict], rule: dict) -> dict:
    """Fill in a version's reward and its verdict against the best complete version before it."""
    per_eval = []
    for entry in record["evals"].values():
        counted = [r for r in entry["runs"] if r["counted"]]
        for r in counted:
            r["reward"] = round(run_reward(r, rule["reward"]), 2)
        entry["reward"] = round(sum(r["reward"] for r in counted) / len(counted), 2) if counted else None
        per_eval.append(entry["reward"])
    record["complete"] = bool(per_eval) and all(value is not None for value in per_eval)
    record["reward"] = round(sum(per_eval) / len(per_eval), 2) if record["complete"] else None
    same = [r for r in earlier if r.get("complete") and sorted(r["evals"]) == sorted(record["evals"])]
    best = max(same, key=lambda r: r["reward"], default=None)
    record["best_before"] = best and {"version": best["version"], "reward": best["reward"]}
    if not record["complete"]:
        record["verdict"] = "incomplete"
    elif best is None:
        record["verdict"] = "first"
    else:
        gain = record["reward"] - best["reward"]
        record["verdict"] = "better" if gain >= rule["min_gain"] else "worse" if gain <= -rule["min_gain"] else "same"
        record["gain"] = round(gain, 2)
    return record


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- runs on the platform


def entry_of(slug: str, entry_id: str) -> dict | None:
    entries = json.loads(atira("eval", "runs", slug, "--json")).get("entries", [])
    return next((e for e in entries if e["id"] == entry_id), None)


def wait(slugs: dict[str, str], repeats: int, minutes: float) -> None:
    """Until every entry has its scored runs, or nothing of it is waiting or running any more. The platform starts a
    run again when it failed one itself, a little after the failure, so an idle entry is looked at twice."""
    deadline, idle = time.time() + minutes * 60, 0
    while time.time() < deadline:
        open_runs, lines = 0, []
        for slug, entry_id in slugs.items():
            runs = (entry_of(slug, entry_id) or {}).get("runs", [])
            scored = sum(r["status"] == "scored" for r in runs)
            busy = sum(r["status"] in WAITING for r in runs)
            if scored < repeats and (busy or not runs):
                open_runs += 1
            lines.append(f"{slug}: {scored}/{repeats} scored, {busy} waiting or running")
        print(time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), "; ".join(lines), flush=True)
        if not open_runs:
            idle += 1
            if idle >= 2:
                return
        else:
            idle = 0
        time.sleep(30)
    print(f"Still running after {minutes:.0f} min; finish later with: python3 dev/trainloop.py collect <version>")


def download(version: str, slug: str, entry_id: str) -> dict:
    """An entry's runs with their scores, and each run's status and timed log in the version's folder."""
    entry = entry_of(slug, entry_id) or {"runs": []}
    folder = TRAIN / version / slug
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    runs = []
    for run in entry["runs"]:
        run_id = run["run_id"]
        (folder / f"{run_id}.json").write_text(atira("status", run_id, "--json", check=False))
        (folder / f"{run_id}.log").write_text(atira("logs", run_id, check=False))  # every line starts with its time
        counted = run["status"] == "scored"
        runs.append({"run_id": run_id, "status": run["status"], "counted": counted, "error": run.get("error"),
                     "quality": run.get("quality"), "eligible": bool(run.get("eligible")),
                     "cost_usd": (run.get("cost_micro_usd") or 0) / 1e6, "seconds": (run.get("duration_ms") or 0) / 1e3,
                     "log": str((folder / f"{run_id}.log").relative_to(ROOT))})
    return {"entry": entry_id, "eval_version": entry.get("version_id"), "runs": runs}


def finish(record: dict) -> int:
    """Download, judge, write the ledger line and print the verdict."""
    rule = json.loads((TRAIN / record["version"] / "rules.json").read_text())
    for slug, entry in record["evals"].items():
        record["evals"][slug] = download(record["version"], slug, entry["entry"])
    earlier = [r for r in ledger() if r["version"] != record["version"]]
    judge(record, earlier, rule)
    with LEDGER.open("a") as out:
        out.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"\n{record['version']}: {record['note']}")
    for slug, entry in record["evals"].items():
        for run in entry["runs"]:
            what = (f"quality {run['quality']}, ${run['cost_usd']:.4f}, {run['seconds']:.0f} s, reward {run['reward']}"
                    if run["counted"] else f"not counted ({run['status']}: {run['error']})")
            print(f"  {slug} {run['run_id']}: {what}\n    log {run['log']}  page https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/"
                  f"{run['run_id']}")
    best = record["best_before"]
    against = f" against {best['reward']} of {best['version']}" if best else ""
    print(f"reward {record['reward']}{against}: {record['verdict'].upper()}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def package(version: str, source: str) -> tuple[str, dict]:
    """What the runs get: a folder with the tracked files of agent/ as they are now, or a platform package id."""
    if source:
        return source, {"package": source}
    folder = TRAIN / version / "package"
    for name in git("ls-files", "agent").splitlines():
        target = folder / name
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copy2(ROOT / name, target)
    return str(folder / "agent"), {"package": "agent/", "commit": git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"),
                                   "branch": git("rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"),
                                   "changed": git("status", "--porcelain", "--", "agent").splitlines()}


def cmd_step(args) -> int:
    rule = rules()
    slugs = args.evals.split(",") if args.evals else rule["evals"]
    repeats = args.repeats or rule["repeats"]
    version = new_version(args.prefix)
    (TRAIN / version).mkdir(parents=True)
    (TRAIN / version / "rules.json").write_text(json.dumps(rule, indent=1))
    what, origin = package(version, args.package)
    record = {"version": version, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()), "note": args.note,
              "repeats": repeats, **origin, "evals": {}}
    for slug in slugs:
        out = atira("eval", "run", slug, "--package", what, "--repeats", str(repeats), "--label", version)
        entry = re.search(r"eve_[0-9a-f]+", out)
        if not entry:
            raise SystemExit(f"No entry id in the answer for {slug}: {out[:300]}")
        record["evals"][slug] = {"entry": entry[0]}
        print(f"{version}: {slug} -> {entry[0]} ({repeats} run{'s' if repeats > 1 else ''})", flush=True)
    (TRAIN / version / "step.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=1))
    wait({slug: e["entry"] for slug, e in record["evals"].items()}, repeats, args.minutes)
    return finish(record)


def cmd_adopt(args) -> int:
    rule = rules()
    found = None
    for slug in (args.evals.split(",") if args.evals else rule["evals"]):
        entry = entry_of(slug, args.entry)
        if entry:
            found = (slug, entry)
    if not found:
        raise SystemExit(f"{args.entry} is not an entry of the evals in {RULES.name}; name its eval with --evals")
    slug, entry = found
    version = new_version(args.prefix)
    (TRAIN / version).mkdir(parents=True)
    (TRAIN / version / "rules.json").write_text(json.dumps(rule, indent=1))
    record = {"version": version, "at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
              "note": args.note or entry.get("label") or "", "repeats": entry.get("repeats", 1),
              "package": entry.get("package", {}).get("sha256", "")[:12], "adopted": entry.get("label"),
              "evals": {slug: {"entry": args.entry}}}
    (TRAIN / version / "step.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=1))
    atira("run", "name", entry["runs"][-1]["run_id"], version, check=False) if entry.get("runs") else None
    return finish(record)


def cmd_collect(args) -> int:
    step = TRAIN / args.version / "step.json"
    if not step.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"No step named {args.version} in {TRAIN.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return finish(json.loads(step.read_text()))


def cmd_report(args) -> int:
    records = sorted(ledger(), key=lambda r: (r["reward"] is None, -(r["reward"] or 0)))
    if not records:
        print("No versions yet: python3 dev/trainloop.py step \"what changed\"")
        return 0
    print(f"{'reward':>7}  {'verdict':10} {'version':32} quality / cost / seconds per counted run; note")
    for r in records:
        runs = [run for e in r["evals"].values() for run in e["runs"] if run["counted"]]
        scores = ", ".join(f"{run['quality']:g} / ${run['cost_usd']:.3f} / {run['seconds']:.0f}" for run in runs)
        reward = "-" if r["reward"] is None else f"{r['reward']:.2f}"
        print(f"{reward:>7}  {r['verdict']:10} {r['version']:32} {scores or 'no counted run'}; {r['note']}")
    return 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    step = commands.add_parser("step")
    step.add_argument("note")
    step.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=0, help="runs per eval, 1 to 3 (default: the rules file's)")
    step.add_argument("--package", default="", help="submission, test, sub_..., run_... (default: agent/ as it is)")
    step.add_argument("--minutes", type=float, default=45, help="how long to wait for the runs")
    adopt = commands.add_parser("adopt")
    adopt.add_argument("entry")
    adopt.add_argument("note", nargs="?", default="")
    collect = commands.add_parser("collect")
    collect.add_argument("version")
    commands.add_parser("report")
    for command in (step, adopt):
        command.add_argument("--evals", default="", help="eval slugs, comma-separated (default: the rules file's)")
        command.add_argument("--prefix", default="train", help="what the version name starts with")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    return {"step": cmd_step, "adopt": cmd_adopt, "collect": cmd_collect, "report": cmd_report}[args.command](args)


if __name__ == "__main__":

The loop tool is built and working: `dev/trainloop.py` with its rule in `dev/train_rules.json`. I tested it on the existing baseline run, and it is now waiting to judge the `main` and `main` + Clef runs, which the platform restarted after its model proxy failed them.

**What one step does**

```sh
python3 dev/trainloop.py step "what changed"
```

1. **Names the version** on the Central European clock, for example `train-20261011-0752-CEST`. It says CEST rather than CET because that is the zone in force today; it will say CET from the winter switch.
2. **Packages `agent/` as it stands** and runs it on the evals in the rules file, with the version name as the run label on the platform.
3. **Waits**, including for runs the platform restarts after its own failures; those failed runs are not counted.
4. **Downloads each run's timed log and score** into `experiments/train/<version>/` (gitignored), next to a copy of the package that ran.
5. **Computes the reward and a verdict** against the best earlier version: BETTER, SAME or WORSE.

**The rule**
- Reward per run = quality (0 if not eligible) − 0.01 × cost × time, using the platform's floors.
- A version's reward is the mean over its evals.
- A version only counts as better or worse if the reward moves by at least 1 point.
- All of that, plus the eval list and repeats, is editable in `dev/train_rules.json`.

**First result**
The current submission on your portal: quality 10, $0.16, 699 s, reward 8.85, recorded as the first baseline. `python3 dev/trainloop.py report` lists every version, best first.

**What it does not do**
- **It measures; it doesn't change the agent.** Deciding what to change between steps is still a person's or my job, by reading the downloaded logs. The fair-play rules apply there: a fix must be general, and nothing seen on the eval sites may go into `agent/`.
- **Each step spends eval runs.** A step costs evals × repeats runs out of the team's shared 12 per hour, so with one eval and one repeat you get at most 12 steps an hour, and teammates use the same budget.
- **One run per version is noisy.** The 1-point threshold is a guess at that noise; with one eval and one repeat, treat small differences as ties.

The tool, the rules file and the `.gitignore` entry are uncommitted on branch `clef-on`, alongside the Clef change. I'll report the `main` versus `main` + Clef comparison when those two runs finish.

content.text:
That log explains the page you saw: your portals were working, and the platform took their addresses away in the middle of the run. Neither of the two train-loop runs is a valid measurement, so I stopped the local waits before they could be recorded as scores.

**What the log shows (the Clef run, started 05:59 UTC)**
- **Up to about 7 minutes in, the sites worked.** The agent was logged in and filling the bid form.
- **Then the addresses died, one site at a time.** The ERP started answering "Nothing is served here" at about 415 s, and the tender portal followed at about 484 s, mid-form.
- **The agent then wasted its remaining budget.** It retried the dead addresses dozens of times and guessed paths like `/dashboard`, `/robots.txt` and `/owncloud/`.
- **Clef did its job, and was ignored.** The `page_check` tool flagged the dead pages as errors with probability 0.99 each time, but the workers kept retrying the same address.

**The other run (plain `main`, started 05:58 UTC)**
It was handed the new addresses, but its sandbox could not connect to them at all (`ERR_TUNNEL_CONNECTION_FAILED`), and it has been retrying the start pages for its whole run. That's why it showed only 3 model calls.

**What I can and can't say about the cause**
- The eval was not redeployed, and all four sites answer 200 at their current addresses right now, so the site code is serving.
- The platform replaced the world's public addresses between about 05:58 and 06:06 UTC. I don't know why, and the eval server's own logs aren't visible to us.
- It could be the platform rollout the organizers mentioned. It could also be a side effect of the cancellations, since `atira cancel` says it removes a run's sandbox. I can't tell from here whether my server process crashed and was restarted; the staggered site failures make a single crash less likely.

**What I'd do next**
1. Ask the organizers why an eval world's addresses change while runs are in flight; that needs fixing on their side or explaining.
2. Wait for the two broken runs to end on their own (I'm not cancelling them, in case cancelling is what triggers this), then rerun both steps with nothing else being cancelled or deployed meanwhile.
3. Separately, the dead-site retry loop is a real agent weakness this exposed: a worker should give up on a site that is gone instead of spending its whole budget on it.

content.text:
The local Clef run finished without a signed bid: the agent researched everything in under 8 minutes, then crashed in the bid form, so there is no agent score for this run.

The preview still shows "quality 100", but that is the expected bid I entered by hand earlier to test the adapter, not the agent's.

**What the agent got right**
All four positions had the correct material, quantity and lead time. That is a big step up from the submission's run on the same portal, which built no positions at all.

**What it got wrong**
- **Discount:** it used 0 % where the expected answer is 5 %. The mail search for the director's approval did not come back with a usable record.
- **Prices and total:** every unit price is about 5 % too high and the total is 341,171.48 against 324,113.38. That follows directly from the missing discount.
- Had it signed this answer, the eval score would have been roughly 73: reference 5, plus 52.5 for the positions (material, quantity and lead time are 70 % of the 75), with discount, prices and total lost.

**Why it crashed**
A newsletter overlay on the bid form covered the "Weiter" button. The click timed out after 5 seconds and the error was not caught, which ended the whole process. This is the same failure the team already noted for this portal in `docs/learned.md`.

**Clef and caching in this run**
- **Clef:** 16 calls, 6,460 input tokens, 18 seconds in total. It judged 11 pages as errors or dead ends and 5 as fine.
- **Cache:** 38 % of input tokens came from the cache (1.28 M of 3.39 M). That's lower than the roughly 60 % per worker seen in the sandbox, but this was a local run through your own proxy, so the two aren't directly comparable.

The two things worth fixing, both general rather than specific to this portal:

1. An overlay that intercepts a click should be closed and the click retried, and a failed click must never end the run.
2. The approval search needs to find the director's mail when records are laid out differently from public-1.

Do you want me to start with the overlay crash? It's the one that turns a roughly 73-point answer into nothing.
now using this changes what do you think we can perform ?

Honestly: the changes made so far (Clef on, the summary lines) probably don't move the score by themselves. The evidence is one run on one portal, so treat everything below as an estimate.

**What the Clef change did in practice**
- Clef answered 16 times in about 1 second each and was right about dead pages, at 0.99 probability each time.
- The workers ignored it and kept retrying the same dead address. A correct second opinion that nobody acts on is worth nothing.
- It didn't prevent the overlay crash or find the missing discount mail.
- So I'd expect Clef as wired today to add a little cost and no points. It would only start paying off if a "dead page" verdict made the worker stop or change approach.

**What we can expect, by dataset**

| Where | Today | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public-1, quality | 100 in roughly 3 of 4 runs | 148 of 201 recorded eligible runs scored 100 |
| Public-1, speed | about 3.5 min, $0.10 on recent `main` | Best soak runs; the submitted version takes 7:33 |
| Your synth portal | 0 as it stands | The one `main` + Clef run crashed before signing |
| Teammates' evals | 0 to 57, one 100 | Recorded eval runs |

**What the two fixes would be worth on your portal**
- **Overlay crash fixed:** the answer that run computed would have scored about 73 instead of nothing.
- **Approval mail found as well:** that same answer becomes 100, since the discount was the only thing wrong.

That is for this one seed. Other seeds use different layouts and rule traps, so I'd expect a spread, not a uniform 100.

**For the final run**
The organizers said most teams dropped on the private dataset, and your eval scores say the same would happen to the current submission. I can't put a number on the private score. What I can say is that fixing general failures, the kind your portals expose, is the only work that raises it, and that Clef and caching tweaks are not where the points are.

One decision for the team, separate from all this: recent `main` is about 2.6 times better than the current submission on cost × time at the same public quality. Submitting it would improve the public rank, but it also replaces the final candidate, so it's worth confirming how it does on the evals first.

import json
rows={}
for l in open("experiments/runs.jsonl"):
    l=l.strip()
    if l:
        try: r=json.loads(l); rows[r["id"]]=r
        except ValueError: pass
def P(r): return r.get("platform") or {}
ok=[r for r in rows.values() if P(r).get("quality")==100 and P(r).get("eligible")]
def secs(r): return P(r).get("scored_duration_s") or r.get("duration_s") or 0
def cost(r): return P(r).get("cost_usd") or 0
print("fastest quality-100 runs:")
for r in sorted(ok,key=secs)[:10]:
    print(f"  {secs(r):5.0f}s ${cost(r):.4f} cxt {max(cost(r),.01)*secs(r):5.1f} req {r.get('requests')} in {r.get('input_tokens')} out {r.get('output_tokens')} {r['id']} {r.get('version')}/{r.get('experiment')} {r.get('commit')} {r.get('started_at','')[5:16]}")
print("cheapest quality-100 runs:")
for r in sorted(ok,key=cost)[:8]:

import statistics
recent=[r for r in ok if (r.get('started_at') or '')>='2026-10-11T03']

EOF

292 and 307 requests ($0.127, $0.145) for 9fb3be4, where the Q&A worker alone used 25 and 28. The 11:12 run lost
  its time to model stalls (a 180 s reader timeout delayed the positions to 262 s, the tender watch fired, and
  verify timed out), not to the Q&A.
- Cost per caller (llm.USAGE, printed after the run summary): Qwen bills uncached input $0.15/M, cached input about
  $0.016/M (cache blocks of 1568 tokens; most calls only reuse the system prompt block) and output $0.47/M. Baseline
  run_92294f32 ($0.145, 297 calls): mail search workers 26 %, ERP detail workers 21 %, ERP/spec readers 11 %, spec
  attempts 9 %, tender workers 7 %, mail readers 6 %. Step count times view size is the lever, not caching.
- Time cuts (cost-cut): the mail planner waited 45 s for tender keys that arrive at ~120 s, so every run planned from
  the brief alone 45 s late; no wait now. verify_board (18-47 s) runs beside the first answer. Six mail tabs instead
  of four. Seven test runs, all 100: 264-381 s against 375-533 s before.
- Mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost end_reserves in one run: keep thinking on.
- ERP hits whose rows contradict the requirement are read only when needed (ERP_DEFER_REST): detail calls 28-32
  instead of 36-53, $0.112-0.129 per run. Records that finished after a requirement's choice were never used anyway.
- cost-cut-2: compact ERP views (gate pages, repeated views, the record banner and tab bars once) halved the
  material reader's text with the same records (8/8 offline); later bid positions entered by the model's mapping
  cut the form worker to 5 calls. The first group search the model makes is repeated for the other groups
  (AGENT_ERP_BATCH): ERP search calls 20-22 -> 4. Detail workers end once open_pages finds no link of their record
  left (ERP_DETAIL_STOP): detail calls 29-39 -> 22-27. Test runs of 4f94f35: 100, 100, 100 at $0.086-0.103.
- Mail search and mail readers are now about half the cost (42-55 %); the next cuts are there.
- A record-level number format comes from a model and does not bind every figure: a soak run (80.1) read an FX
  fixing tagged "de" whose rate was written with a decimal point, parsed it as ten thousand times the rate and bid
  three USD positions at millions of EUR. A separator that cannot group thousands is now the decimal mark, and a
  base price more than 100x (or under 1/1000) its ERP per-piece price is blanked and sends FX to the gap pass.
- Cheaper own-key models on OpenRouter (model-qwen3.7-flash, model-gpt-oss-120b): neither keeps quality. Qwen3.7
  Flash (only Alibaba serves it; not Fireworks) scored 21.7, 59.9 and 72 in 10-16 min for $0.039-0.051; its
  thinking-off tender worker re-requested the TAN instead of submitting, so two runs looped through TAN requests
  until the deadline, and research missed the discount, total and metal index window. GPT-OSS-120B (DeepInfra)
  scored 10: no positions by the answer deadline, thinking-on calls hit the 180 s timeout. Hosted Qwen stays.
- OpenRouter reasoning for Qwen: {"effort": "low", "exclude": true} still bills 2,000-4,000 hidden reasoning tokens
  per call (23-43 s); {"enabled": false} gives 0. Qwen3.7 Flash prices triple above 32k prompt tokens.
