Context: `agent/` is a pydantic-ai web agent (hosted Qwen) that researches four websites and enters a bid. We want to cut wall time and model cost of the MAIL research, which is the biggest cost. A measured good run: research finishes at ~120 s; the model-call table shows "worker mail Summary" = 90 calls, all with thinking on, 366k input tokens, 39% of run cost, and "research_mail.read_message" = 14 thinking calls, 11% of cost. Six mail tabs each run one "record kind" search at a time (approval, end_reserves, condition_rules, packaging, commitments, fx, setup_pools, project_bonus, metal_indices), each taking 26-87 s and 7-14 requests. A note in docs/learned.md says mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost a record, so thinking stays on.

Please report, with file paths and line numbers:
1. In `agent/research_mail.py` (and what it calls in `agent/orchestrator.py`, `agent/site_tools.py`, `agent/worker.py`, `agent/browser_tools.py`): the exact flow of one record-kind search. Who plans the kinds (function name), what the per-kind goal prompt is, which tools the search worker has (search, collect/collect_pages, extract, open, etc.), what a worker returns, how messages get read (`read_message`), and what budgets/limits apply (request limits, deadlines, tab count constants, env switches such as AGENT_* / MAIL_*).
2. Whether there is any existing mechanism to (a) search once for the tender reference and classify all hits for several kinds in one model call, (b) reuse a result list across kinds, (c) read several messages in one model call, (d) run a kind with thinking off. Name the functions/flags if they exist.
3. What "collect_pages" / pagination helpers do and whether their output (the list rows) is kept in the model context in full.
4. Which unit tests cover mail research (files under `agent/tests/`) and which dev scripts exercise it offline (`dev/research_check*.py` etc.), with how to run them.
5. Any comments or docs/learned.md bullets that explain why the design is one-worker-per-kind, or that warn against merging kinds (quote the lines briefly).

content.text:
I'm in plan mode, so nothing is being changed. Two read-only explorations are mapping where the time and cost go (mail research, and the bid form and signing); I'll build the plan from their findings.

What the numbers already say about reaching 3rd:

- **The bar:** BaoByte in 3rd is at cost × time 3.9 ($0.033 × 1:56). Your best recorded run is 19.3.
- **2:20 alone isn't enough:** at today's cost of about $0.09, a 2:20 run comes to about 12.6, which is 4th or 5th. The run log has no 2:20 run; the fastest recorded full-score run is 3:19.
- **What 3rd needs:** for example 2:00 at $0.032, or 1:40 at $0.038. That means roughly a third of today's cost and about half the time, together.

Where a good run spends its 3:49 and $0.09:

| Phase | Wall time | Share of cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research (mail search is the long pole) | 0:00–2:00 | Mail search 39 %, mail reading 11 %, ERP and spec about 30 % |
| Filling the bid form | 2:00–3:21 | About 3 %, almost all browser time |
| Review, TAN and submit | 3:21–3:49 | Small |

So the two levers are the mail research (half the cost, and it sets when research ends) and the 80 seconds of form filling that use almost no model time.

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>No mechanism exists today for any of (a)–(d): every kind is its own thinking-on worker run, and every kept message is its own thinking-on reader call. Everything below is from reading the code on `clef-on`; nothing was run.

## 1. Flow of one record-kind search

**Planning**
- `plan_searches()` in `agent/research_mail.py:282-330` makes one model call with thinking off (`PLAN_TIMEOUT` 30 s, retries 3) and returns a `SearchPlan` of `PlannedSearch` items.
- Each item becomes a `Kind` (name, subject, sender, sender_form, site, what, schema; `:245-254`), chosen from the nine `SCHEMAS` (`:229-242`), deduped and sorted approval-first.
- It is called from `Orchestrator._plan_mail()` (`agent/orchestrator.py:702-722`): a quick try at 30 s per call within a 75 s budget, then a patient try at `PLAN_PATIENT_TIMEOUT` 90 s.
- `Orchestrator.mails()` (`:673-700`) starts the `MAIL_TABS` sign-ins, staggered 4 s apart (`_mail_tab`, `:724`), while the plan runs.

**Scheduling**
- `Orchestrator._research_mail()` (`orchestrator.py:745-812`) queues the kinds in the order approval, end_reserves, condition_rules, then the rest.
- Each tab loops: pop a kind, then `research_mail.research_kind(session, kind, reference, deadline=, seconds=budget)`.
- The budget comes from `_kind_seconds()` (`:728-734`): mail time left divided by rounds, clamped to 120–240 s.
- A kind that stopped with nothing is re-queued once if more than `MAIL_RETRY_SECONDS` (90 s) remain (`:789-796`).
- `research_mail.research_mail()` (`research_mail.py:887-917`) is a simpler copy of this loop, used only by the dev script.

**Per-kind goal prompt**: `_goal(kind, reference, again)` at `research_mail.py:333-346`.
```
Find every message on this website that is this record, for tender {reference}: {kind.what}
- Search for the exact reference {reference} together with the word {kind.subject!r}.
- Each time a result list shows hits whose subject is this record for exactly {reference}, call keep_results
  RIGHT AWAY with those exact subjects ... Older and newer versions share a subject; keep_results keeps all.
- If the hits span several pages, call collect_pages with the ref of the list's next-page control first.
- Check every folder the mailbox has (e.g. inbox and archive) once, with the same search. ...
As soon as every folder is checked, return a one-line summary. Do not open messages yourself, do not use back()
and do not note() anything: kept messages are read for you.
```
The first prompt is this goal plus the full current view, under the generic `worker.INSTRUCTIONS` (`worker.py:25-51`).

**Search worker**: `_search()` at `research_mail.py:499-541` calls `run_worker(session, goal, Summary, deadline=until, max_steps=20, thinking=True, grounded=False, tools=(paging_tool(Collected()), keep_messages_tool(kept)))`.
- Its tools are the browser `TOOLS` (`browser_tools.py:924`: goto, click, fill, select, options, check, back, read_more, note), plus `collect_pages`, `keep_results`, and `page_check` when Clef is on (`clef.tools()`, `clef.py:146`).
- It does not have `site_tools.search/collect/extract`; `SITE_TOOLS` (`site_tools.py:740`) is not passed. The model types the query with `fill(..., submit=true)`.
- `note` stays registered even though the goal forbids it (`notes=True` is the default).
- It returns `Summary(summary: str)` (`research_tender.py:62`), which is discarded. The real output is the side effect on `kept`; `_search` returns only "done", "ended" or "stalled".
- The usage label is `"worker mail Summary"` (`worker.py:208`), which is the 90-call row in your table.

**keep_results** (`keep_messages_tool`, `research_mail.py:426-457`)
- The model passes exact link texts. The tool matches them against every link in `session.seen` (all views the tab ever showed), keeps same-host URLs, caps at 20, and opens them in parallel temporary tabs via `open_message()` (`:397-423`).
- `open_message` also opens empty reading-pane frames and retries once on a sign-in redirect.
- The tool returns only `Kept n of m` plus two header lines per message.

**Reading** (`_Reading.append`, `:460-475`; `read_message`, `:370-388`)
- Each kept view immediately spawns one `read_message` task: one model call per message, thinking on, `READ_TIMEOUT` 60 s, retries 3, output `MailRecord[kind.schema.content]`.
- An `ungrounded()` validator raises `ModelRetry`, which costs an extra call each time it fires.
- The prompt is `READ_INSTRUCTIONS` (`:349-355`) plus the whole message page view.
- Reads run alongside the ongoing search.

**research_kind** (`:558-600`): `_usable` → `_search` → if nothing kept, one more `_search` with the `again` hint (or on a fresh tab after a stall) → wait for reads → `KindResult(kind, kept, records, seconds, stopped)`.

**Resolution** is mechanical: `resolve_mail()` (`:864-884`) → `valid_records` / `latest_per_key` / `_apply`.

**Budgets and limits**

| Limit | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Worker request limit | 20 (`UsageLimits(request_limit=max_steps)`), tool retries 4 | `research_mail.py:507`, `worker.py:187,213` |
| `KIND_SECONDS` | 150 s, when no `seconds` is passed | `research_mail.py:56` |
| Orchestrator per-kind budget | 120–240 s (`KIND_MIN_SECONDS` / `KIND_MAX_SECONDS`) | `orchestrator.py:62-63` |
| `MIN_KIND_SECONDS` | 50 s | `research_mail.py:57` |
| `STALL_SECONDS` | 45 s, then a fresh tab | `:58` |
| `KEEP_GRACE` | 60 s after the first kept hit, then the search is cut | `:59`, `:516` |
| `READ_RESERVE` | 25 s | `:60` |
| `RETRY_SECONDS` | 90 s | `:61` |
| `READ_TIMEOUT` / `PLAN_TIMEOUT` | 60 s / 30 s | `:62-63` |
| `MAX_VIEW` | 14,000 chars per page view | `browser_tools.py:24` |
| `MAX_RETURN` / `MAX_PAGES` (paging tool) | 30,000 chars / 40 pages | `research_tender.py:39-40` |

**Env switches**
- `MAIL_TABS` (default 6, `orchestrator.py:56`) and `AGENT_MAIL_SECONDS` (540, `:66`).
- `AGENT_FINDINGS_WAIT` (0, `:71`) and `AGENT_GAP_REWORK` (`:75`).
- `AGENT_CLEF` / `USE_CLEF` (`clef.py:30`).
- `LLM_TIMEOUT`, `LLM_TIMEOUT_THINKING`, `LLM_RETRIES`, `LLM_HEDGE_AFTER` (`llm.py:84-115`).
- There are no `MAIL_*` switches for thinking or batching. `llm.thinking(phase, default)` (`llm.py:738`, `THINKING_<PHASE>`) exists but is not wired into the mail search or reader.

## 2. Existing mechanisms

- **(a) One search, classify hits for several kinds in one call:** none. `Kind`, `_goal`, `_Reading` and `read_message` are all single-kind.
- **(b) Reuse a result list across kinds:** not by design.
  - `Collected()` is created fresh per `_search`.
  - Incidentally, `keep_results` matches against `session.seen`, which persists per tab across kinds. A later kind on the same tab can keep a link an earlier kind's list showed, but the model is never shown those earlier lists.
  - Nothing is shared between tabs.
- **(c) Several messages in one model call:** none. It is one `read_message` per kept view; `gaps.reread()` (`agent/gaps.py:471`) also calls it per view.
- **(d) A kind with thinking off:** no flag. `thinking=True` is hard-coded at `research_mail.py:507` (search) and `:373` (reader). The plumbing exists (`run_worker(thinking=...)`, `llm.thinking("…", default)`), so it would be a one-line switch.

## 3. `collect_pages` and pagination helpers

**`paging_tool(collected, thorough=False)` → `collect_pages(next_ref)`** (`research_tender.py:307-371`) is the one mail uses.
- The model names the next/load-more control. The helper clicks it up to 40 times, polling up to 4 × 0.7 s per page, and stores each full page view in `Collected.pages`.
- It returns the whole list as concatenated full page views (`=== page view i` plus the entire view, folders and chrome included), capped at 30,000 chars.
- These are raw views, not compact rows.

**Context retention** (`worker._forget_old_views`, `worker.py:87-108`)
- Only the latest view-bearing message is kept in full; older ones shrink to stubs.
- The `collect_pages` result contains `URL:\nTitle:` headers, so it counts as the latest view.
- The `keep_results` return has no such header (`_heads` joins with " / "). So after collect → keep, the collected text of up to 30k chars is re-sent in full on every later request until the model navigates to another folder.
- `collect_pages` is not in `KEEP_RESULTS = {"search","collect","extract"}` (`worker.py:60`), so it is stubbed entirely once a newer view arrives.

**`site_tools.paginate` / `search` / `collect`** (`site_tools.py:288-485`) are not used by mail.
- They return compact numbered rows (`ROW_CHARS` 300, `MAX_ROWS` 200, `MAX_PAGES` 25) with link targets.
- Their results stay in context up to `KEEP_CHARS` 12,000.
- Note that `keep_results` only finds links in `session.seen` in the `[eN link "text" -> href]` form, and `site_tools._format` rows use a different format (`["name" -> href]`), though `paginate` does run every page through `session.look()`.

## 4. Tests and dev scripts

**Unit tests** (offline, no model): run with `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)`, or a single file with `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_research_mail`.
- `agent/tests/test_research_mail.py`: `MailDomainTest`, `KindBudgetTest` (`kind_budget`, approval-first), `ConversionTest` (fx, metal index, calc mapping), `SenderTest`, `SeveralKeysTest`, `LandedTest`.
- `agent/tests/test_orchestrator.py:277` `MailPlan` covers the `_plan_mail` quick-then-patient timeouts.
- `agent/tests/test_gaps.py` covers mail gaps and rework.
- `agent/tests/test_tender_qa.py:343-367` covers `resolve_mail` with reserves.
- Nothing tests `_goal`, `_search`, `keep_results`, `read_message` or `_forget_old_views` for mail.

**Dev scripts**: none of these is truly offline; they need the scouting logins and the model proxy.
- `dev/research_check_records.py [tender|mail]` is the mail-only harness. It runs `plan_searches` plus `research_mail.research_mail` and prints records and timings.
  - Run: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"; HEADLESS=1 MAIL_TABS=6 uv run --project agent python dev/research_check_records.py mail`
  - Its `MAIL_TABS` default is 5 and `CHECK_SECONDS` default is 600.
  - It uses `research_mail()`, not the orchestrator loop, so `KIND_SECONDS` 150 applies and there is no 120–240 s sharing.
- `dev/site_tools_check.py --mail-topic WORD --only mail` compares a mailbox search with and without `SITE_TOOLS`.
- `dev/local-soak.sh` and `dev/run-local.sh` do full local runs up to signing.
- `dev/research_check.py` is spec and ERP only.

## 5. Why one worker per kind

No comment or doc line explicitly warns against merging kinds. The design is described rather than argued:
- `research_mail.py:5-7`: "Per kind a worker (one tab each) chooses its searches and folders; `collect_pages` pages through a result list it points at and `keep_results` opens the hits whose subject it names (only links it has actually seen)."
- `orchestrator.py:54-55`: "about nine record kinds took three rounds over four tabs ... six tabs take them in two rounds (tabs are free, the work and its cost stay the same)."

Relevant warnings in `docs/learned.md`:
- `:250` "Mail search with thinking off took 211 calls instead of 85 and lost end_reserves in one run: keep thinking on."
- `:136-137` "One run with the mail kinds on site_tools.search/collect kept nothing in three kinds (150 s each; paging followed a message list into a session expiry); kept on the paging tool for now."
- `:122` "Mail kinds that find nothing burn the full 20-step budget (about 70 s per kind and tab)."
- `:246` "Step count times view size is the lever, not caching."
- `:258` "Mail search and mail readers are now about half the cost (42-55 %); the next cuts are there."
- `:156-160` gives the history of pipelined reads, the 60 s grace, the 45 s stall and reopen-on-redirect.

## Fair-play constraint

`CLAUDE.md:72-75`: "Must be agentic: a model chooses where to go, what to search and what matters. Rejected: a fixed click path ... or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation. Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms."

Helpers that rely on "paginate a model-selected result set":
- `collect_pages` (`research_tender.paging_tool`): the model names the next control.
- `site_tools.paginate`, `search` / `run_search` and `collect`: the model picks the field, query and list.

Helpers that rely on "parse a page the model chose":
- `keep_results` → `open_message`: the model names the subjects.
- `read_message`.
- `research_tender.keep_tool` / `open_and_keep`.

A related precedent is `AGENT_ERP_BATCH` (`research.py:864`, `learned.md:254`): the model's first ERP search is repeated by the harness for the other groups.

For a merged design, the model would still have to choose the query and folders and name which subjects belong to which kind. A helper that sweeps all folders for the reference before any model call is the rejected crawler pattern.

## Most promising cuts

1. **Multi-kind search worker** — `_goal()`, `_search()`, `keep_messages_tool()`, `_Reading` (`research_mail.py:333-541`) and the queue in `Orchestrator._research_mail()` (`orchestrator.py:745`).
   - One worker would get several kinds, search the reference once per folder, and call `keep_results(kind, link_texts)` per kind.
   - This removes the repeated search / folder-switch / collect steps that make up most of the 90 calls; the 60 s `KEEP_GRACE` and the 20-request cap would need rescaling.
   - It is still model-directed; keep 2–3 groups across tabs for parallelism and loss isolation.
2. **Shrink what is re-sent each step** — `paging_tool.collect_pages` return (`research_tender.py:363-367`) and `worker._forget_old_views` / `_shrink` (`worker.py:64-108`).
   - Return compact rows (subject, sender, date, link) instead of up to 30k chars of raw views that stay as the latest view through every later step.
   - Any change must keep the `[eN link "…" -> href]` form in `session.seen` so `keep_results` still matches.
3. **Batch the reader** — `read_message()` and `_Reading.append()` (`research_mail.py:370-388`, `:460-475`).
   - Read all messages kept by one `keep_results` call in one model call returning `list[MailRecord]`.
   - Separately, strip page furniture (folder list, message list) in `open_message()` before reading.
   - That targets the 14 thinking calls and their input; `gaps.reread()` shares the function.
4. **End the worker sooner** — `_search()` stop logic (`research_mail.py:516`) and `_goal`.
   - `KEEP_GRACE` is a fixed 60 s after the first hit and the worker otherwise runs to 20 requests.
   - A harness stop once every folder the mailbox shows has had a completed search (in the style of `ERP_DETAIL_STOP`) would trim tail steps.

# Plan: cut cost x time toward 3rd place, staged and safe first

## Context

The public leaderboard ranks teams at quality 100 by cost x time. Third place (BaoByte) is at 3.9
($0.033 x 1:56). Our submission is at 49.7; the best recorded run of recent `main` is 19.3 ($0.097 x 3:19), which
would be 5th. No 2:20 run is in `experiments/runs.jsonl`, and 2:20 at today's cost would still be about 12.6.

Third needs roughly a third of today's cost and half the time together. A measured good run
(`run_c7403cf6df6fe24c`, 229 s, $0.090) spends them like this:

| Phase | Wall time | Cost share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Research; the last mail kind ends it | 0-120 s | mail search 39 %, mail readers 11 %, ERP/spec ~30 % |
| Bid form after research | 120-201 s (80 s, only 5 model calls) | ~3 % |
| Review, TAN, submit | 201-228 s | small |

Decisions taken with the user: staged, low-risk cuts first; every change proven on public-1 (3 test runs at 100)
and on the evals (no drop); stop and report before any `atira submit`, since it replaces the final-run candidate.

Honest expectation: stage 1 lands around cost x time 10-13 (4th-5th). Stage 2 gets to roughly 6-8. Reaching under
3.9 needs stage 3 to work as well, and the teams ahead keep moving. Each stage is worth having on its own.

## Where the work goes

New branch `speed-cuts` off `main` (not `clef-on`: Clef adds calls and no points so far; it stays its own branch).
Carry over only the cache-share line in `llm.usage_table()` from `clef-on`, because it is used for measuring.
Commit per measured change, team conventions (author `josteng`, no trailers), no push without asking.

## Stage 1: low-risk cuts (no change to what the model decides)

Bid form and signing, `agent/submit.py`, `agent/configurator.py`, `agent/browser_tools.py`:

1. **Click that cannot crash the run.** `submit.py:454` clicks the next button outside the `try`; a covered button
   raised through the worker and restarted the whole form (seen on our synth portal). Give it the same fallback
   as `browser_tools._click` (overlay closed by the existing helper, then a JS click) and catch the timeout.
   Reliability first; this is the fix that turns a 0 into a signed bid on unfamiliar forms.
2. **Light settle inside the scripted position loop.** `configurator._confirm` (470-479) and
   `PositionDesk._enter` run a full `SiteSession.settle()` per cascade level: `networkidle` 2.5 s plus the
   login/cookies/error/human-check sweep. Add a light mode to `settle`/`_settle` (`browser_tools.py:487, 552`)
   that waits for the next control or a page change, and falls back to the full settle on any failure.
   Estimated 15-35 s of the 80 s.
3. **Drop duplicate looks.** `fill_position` returns its last view; `_enter` and `_continue` reuse it instead of
   calling `session.look()` again (`submit.py:348, 417, 443, 460`; `configurator.py:504`). Estimated 3-8 s.
4. **Shorter TAN round trip.** Add `fill_in` to the sign pass tools (`submit.py:757-758`) so TAN entry and submit
   are one model step, and start the mail reload in `request_signing_tan` (667) right after the click.
   Estimated 4-7 s.
5. **Warm mail tab.** `Mailbox` gets the same in-tab keepalive as `BidFlow._keep_alive` (934), so `_tan` reloads a
   signed-in inbox. Small typical gain, removes the 150 s tail noted in `docs/learned.md:215`.

Mail research, `agent/research_mail.py`, `agent/research_tender.py`, `agent/worker.py`:

6. **Compact result lists.** `collect_pages` (`research_tender.py:307-371`) returns up to 30,000 characters of raw
   page views that are re-sent on every later step. Return compact rows (subject, sender, date, link) in the
   `[eN link "..." -> href]` form that `keep_results` matches against `session.seen`.
7. **Batch the reader.** `read_message` (370-388) is one thinking call per kept message (14 calls, 11 % of cost).
   Read the messages kept by one `keep_results` call in one call returning a list of `MailRecord`, with the same
   grounding validator; `gaps.reread()` keeps the single-message path.
8. **End a search sooner.** Pass `notes=False` (the goal already forbids `note`/`back`), and stop the worker once
   each folder the mailbox shows has had a completed search, in the style of `ERP_DETAIL_STOP`
   (`_search`, 499-541; `KEEP_GRACE` at 516).

Not doing: thinking off for the mail search (`docs/learned.md:250`: 211 calls instead of 85 and a lost record).

## Stage 2: mail search covering several kinds (only if stage 1 holds 100)

One worker takes a small group of record kinds, searches the reference once per folder and calls
`keep_results(kind, link_texts)` per kind. Touches `_goal` (333), `_search`, `keep_messages_tool` (426),
`_Reading`, and the queue in `Orchestrator._research_mail` (`orchestrator.py:745-812`). Keep two or three groups on
separate tabs for parallelism and so one failed group cannot lose every record; rescale `KEEP_GRACE` and the
20-request cap. Behind a switch (`AGENT_MAIL_GROUPS`, default off until proven) so it can be compared and reverted.

Fair play: the model still chooses the query and folders and names which subjects belong to which kind. No helper
may sweep folders before a model call.

## Stage 3: only if stages 1 and 2 are proven and the gap to 3rd is still open

- ERP detail and spec readers (about 30 % of cost): same treatment as mail (compact views, fewer steps).
- Enter the on-screen position's material cascade as soon as materials are chosen, before prices. Needs a hook from
  `Orchestrator.select_materials` to `BidFlow`, a no-save mode in `_enter`, and partial entries past
  `configurator.complete_positions` (243). Riskiest item: unsaved state dies with the session and a choice can
  still change.

## Verification (per change, then per stage)

1. Unit tests: `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)`; new cases beside
   `tests/test_auto_positions.py`, `tests/test_form_shapes.py`, `tests/test_signing.py`,
   `tests/test_research_mail.py` for the click fallback, light settle, batched reader and compact rows.
2. Offline form check: `dev/configurator_check.py` on the mock wizard; mail-only harness:
   `dev/research_check_records.py mail` (needs the scouting logins and `atira models proxy`).
3. Public-1: three `dev/test-run.sh v2 "<change>" <experiment>` runs; all three must score 100. Compare the
   phase times in the run summary and the per-caller table against `run_c7403cf6df6fe24c`.
4. Evals: `python3 dev/trainloop.py step "<change>"` with `dev/train_rules.json` listing `err404-synth-hazards-0`,
   `err404-traps`, `err404-layout`, `err404-nobid`; the reward must not drop against the `main` baseline step.
   Take the baseline step first. The platform has been failing eval runs on its side today; failed runs are not
   counted and are rerun.
5. Record every run (`experiments/runs.jsonl` via the dev scripts) and add a `docs/learned.md` bullet per result.

Run budget: 12 concurrent runs and 12 eval runs an hour are shared with the team; a full check is 3 test runs plus
4 eval runs, so coordinate before starting a round.

## Stop points

- After stage 1 and after stage 2: report quality, cost, time, cost x time and eval reward, and wait.
- No `atira submit` and no promotion of a test run without the team's confirmation.

        value name. `confirm_button`: label of the button that applies a choice so the next choice opens.
        `next_button`: label of the button that saves the position and goes on (never one that omits or adds).
        """
        problems = mapping_problems(ctx.deps.session.view, fields or {}, self.known, (confirm_button, next_button))
        if problems:
            return "Not taken: " + "; ".join(problems) + ". Fix the mapping and call again."
        self.remember(fields, confirm_button, next_button)
        ctx.deps.session.trace.event(ctx.deps.session.name, "position_form_mapped", fields=self.plan.fields,
                                     confirm=self.plan.confirm, next=self.next_button)
        return "Mapping taken. Enter nothing on this page; return now."

    async def configure_position(self, ctx: RunContext[Deps], position: str, fields: dict[str, str] | None = None,
                                 confirm_button: str = "", next_button: str = "",
                                 choices: dict[str, str] | None = None, entered_yourself: bool = False) -> str:
        """
        Enter all values of the position the form shows now and, once all are in, save it and go on with the form's
        next/continue button. `position`: its number as the page shows it. `fields`: control label (exactly as in
        your view) -> value name; needed on the first call, later calls reuse it. `confirm_button`: label of the
        button that applies a choice so the next choice opens. `next_button`: label of the button that saves the
        position and goes on (never the one that omits or adds a position); needed once. `choices`: only when a
        call reported it: control label -> the option to choose. `entered_yourself`: True only after you entered
        a position yourself because this tool handed it to you.
        """
        session, plan, asked = ctx.deps.session, self.plan, position.strip()
        self.sync(session)

        def refuse(reason: str, text: str) -> str:  # every early return is traced: the run logs show why
            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_refused", position=asked, reason=reason,
                                fields=fields or {}, text=text[:300])
            return text

        if entered_yourself:
            done = next((p for p in self.handed if p == asked or re.search(
                r"(?<![\w.])" + re.escape(p) + r"(?![\w]|\.\d)", asked)), None)
            if done is None:
                return refuse("not_handed", "Only a position this tool handed to you counts as entered by you; "
                                            "call configure_position() for the others.")
            self.entered.add(done)
            session.trace.event(session.name, "entered_by_model", position=done)
            return f"Position {done} counted as entered. {self.so_far(session)} Still to enter: {self.remaining()}."
        unknown = self.remember(fields, confirm_button, next_button)
        if unknown:
            return refuse("unknown_names", unknown)
        async with session.lock:
            view = await session.look()
            position, shown = resolve_position(asked, self.entries, view)
            if position is None or position not in shown:  # a page between two states: look again once settled
                await session.settle()
                view = await session.look()
                position, shown = resolve_position(asked, self.entries, view)
        if position is None:
            if shown:  # several of the bid's positions on one page: the model must name one of them
                return refuse("ambiguous", f"Name the position this page is about by its own number (one of "
                                           f"{', '.join(shown)}), then call again.")
            return refuse("no_values", f"No values for position {asked!r} (the page shows none of this bid's "
                                       f"positions {', '.join(sorted(self.entries, key=position_key))}): leave it "
                                       f"out with the form's option to omit a position. {self.so_far(session)}")
        if position not in shown:
            return refuse("not_on_page", f"Position {position} is not on the page now. Configure the position "
                                         "the page shows, by its own number; omit only a position that is not one "
                                         f"of {self.remaining()}.")
        if not plan.fields:
            return refuse("no_fields", f"Position {position} has values to enter. Give fields (control label -> "
                                       f"value name) for the controls of this form, then call again; do not omit it.")
        if position in self.handed:
            return refuse("handed", self.hand_over(position, session))
        if self.failures.get(position, 0) >= 3:
            return refuse("failed", f"Position {position} failed three times: leave it out with the form's option "
                                    f"to omit a position. {self.so_far(session)}")
        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline - self.reserve:
            return refuse("time", "Time is short: leave this and every remaining position out and go on to "
                                  "signing. " + self.so_far(session))
        entry = self.entries[position]
        values, labels = unmapped(view, entry, plan.fields)
        if values and labels and not self.asked_unmapped:  # asked once per run; the next call fills as mapped
            self.asked_unmapped = True
            return refuse("unmapped", f"Nothing entered yet. This bid has values for {', '.join(values)}, but no "
                                      f"control is mapped to them, while these fields of the page are not mapped: "
                                      f"{'; '.join(labels)}. Call again now with fields that add every one of them "
                                      "that takes such a value (the mapping you gave stays); leave out fields that "
                                      "match none.")
        self.layout = page_layout(view)
        text, saved = await self._enter(session, position, shown, asked, choices)
        if saved and AUTO_POSITIONS:
            text = await self._continue(session, text)
        return text

    def _auto_blocker(self, position: str | None, shown: list[str], view: str) -> str:
        """Why the next page is not entered with the mapping the model gave ('' when it can be): it must show
        exactly one bid position not yet entered, with the same controls (kinds and labels) as the position page the
        model named showed before it was filled, and time must be left."""
        if position is None or shown != [position]:
            return "the page shows no single bid position"
        if position in self.entered or position in self.handed or self.failures.get(position):
            return f"position {position} was entered or tried before"
        if not self.next_button:
            return "no save button named"
        if time.monotonic() > self.deadline - self.reserve:
            return "time"
        layout = page_layout(view)
        if layout != self.layout:
            return f"other controls: {sorted(layout ^ self.layout)[:6]}"
        return ""

    async def _continue(self, session, text: str) -> str:
        """
        After a position was entered and saved: the next position pages are entered with the same mapping as long
        as each one passes _auto_blocker; fill_position checks every option and value, and a failure or a page
        that does not pass goes back to the model with the latest result.
        """
        done: list[str] = []
        while True:
            async with session.lock:
                view = await session.look()
            position, shown = resolve_position("", self.entries, view)
            blocker = self._auto_blocker(position, shown, view)
            if blocker:
                session.trace.event(session.name, "auto_positions_stop", entered=done, reason=blocker[:200])
                break
            text, saved = await self._enter(session, position, shown, position, None)
            done.append(position)
            if not saved:
                break
        if not done:
            return text
        return f"Entered with the same mapping as well: {', '.join(done)}. " + text

    async def _enter(self, session, position: str, shown: list[str], asked: str,
                     choices: dict[str, str] | None) -> tuple[str, bool]:
        """Fill one position page and save it: the tool's message, and whether it was entered and saved."""
        plan, entry = self.plan, self.entries[position]
        async with session.lock:
            log: list[str] = []
            try:
                error = await fill_position(session, entry, plan, log, self.picks(position, entry, choices))
            except Exception as exc:  # a slow or changed page: the model decides to retry or omit
                error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:200]}"
            moved, saved = "", False
            if not error and self.next_button:  # the model named the button; clicking it is the mechanical part
                view = await session.look()
                ref, why = find_control(view, self.next_button, ("button",))
                target = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None
                target, own = await scoped(session, target, position)
                others = [p for p in shown if p != position and p not in self.entered]
                if target is None:
                    moved = f" Could not save it: {why}; click the form's next/continue button yourself."
                elif others and not own:  # the page's button would leave the other positions it lists unentered
                    moved = (f" This page also shows {', '.join(others)}: enter each with configure_position(); "
                             f"{self.next_button!r} is clicked after the last of them.")
                else:
                    await target.click(timeout=5000)
                    await session.settle()
                    moved = f" Saved with {self.next_button!r}; the page below is the form's next step."
                    saved = True
            session.trace.event(session.name, "configure_position", position=position, done=log, error=error,
                                moved=moved)
            view = await session.look()
        if error:
            self.failures[position] = self.failures.get(position, 0) + 1
            self.entered.discard(position)
            if NUMBER_ONLY not in error:  # the form, not the value, stood in the way
                self.form_failures[position] = self.form_failures.get(position, 0) + 1
            if self.form_failures.get(position, 0) >= HAND_OVER_AFTER:
                self.handed.add(position)
                session.trace.event(session.name, "handed_to_model", position=position, error=error[:300])
                return (f"Position {position} not entered: {error}. {self.hand_over(position, session)}\n\n{view}",
                        False)

async def holds_option(element, kind: str, option: dict) -> bool:
    """Whether the choice control shows `option` as chosen."""
    if kind == "select":
        return await element.evaluate("e => e.value") == option["value"]
    if kind == "combobox":
        shown = clean(await element.evaluate(SHOWN_JS))
        if shown and clean(option["text"]) in shown:

    options = await element.evaluate(OPTIONS_JS, await _ref(element))

def choice_hint(view: str, plan: FillPlan, picked: dict[str, str], entry: dict) -> str:
    """
    The page's choices that no value is mapped to (a series or group that narrows the next list), with their
    options, for the model to pick through `choices`; '' when there are none.
    """
    mapped = {clean(label) for label in plan.fields} | set(picked)
    lines = []
    for element in ELEMENT.findall(view):
        found = CONTROL.match(element)
        if not found or found.group(2) not in CHOICE_KINDS or clean(found.group(3)) in mapped:
            continue
        options = element.split(" options: ", 1)[1].rstrip("]") if " options: " in element else ""
        lines.append(f"{found.group(3)!r}" + (f" (options: {options[:300]})" if options else ""))
    if not lines:
        return ""
    answer_keys = MONEY_KEYS | COUNT_KEYS | {"material_number", "position"}
    wanted = ", ".join(f"{k} {v}" for k, v in entry.items() if k not in answer_keys)
    return (f" No value is mapped to these choices of the page: {'; '.join(lines)}. If one of them must be set "
            f"first, call again with choices={{label: the option that fits this position"
            f"{f' ({wanted})' if wanted else ''}}}.")

    target = await locate(session.page, button) if button else None
    target, _ = await scoped(session, target, position)
    if target is None:
        return view, why or f"{plan.confirm!r} vanished from the page"
    await target.click(timeout=5000)
    await session.settle()
    return await session.look(), None


async def fill_position(session, entry: dict, plan: FillPlan, log: list[str],

    """
    Enter one position's values into the form on screen, control by control in page order; returns an error
    message, or None when every mapped control holds its value.

    A choice (select, combobox, listbox, radio group) mapped to a material attribute (a key that is not an answer
    field) narrows the next one: after setting it, `plan.confirm` is clicked so the page offers the next level, and
    the choice must survive that round trip. A control still disabled (a choice from an earlier visit not yet
    confirmed) gets one confirm. `choices` (label -> option text) is the model's pick for such a choice, used where

    needs); numbers must match exactly, and answer fields are never overridden. On a page with several positions,
    every control comes from the row or card of this position.

    # a position counts as entered only with its material, quantity, price and lead time (the material control
    # opens only once the choices before it are made)

    steps += [(label, None) for label in (choices or {}) if clean(label) not in mapped]

            if (option is None and key is not None and key not in answer_keys and clean(label) in picked

                shown = " | ".join(o["text"] for o in options if o["value"])[:600]
                worded = key is not None and key not in answer_keys and parse_number(value) is None
                if worded:
                    hint = (f" If one option means the same as {value!r}, call again with choices={{{label!r}: "
                            f"<that option>}}.")

                    hint = choice_hint(view, plan, picked, entry) or " " + NUMBER_ONLY

            if error:

            kept = await locate(session.page, ref) if ref else None

            if kept is None or not await holds_option(kept, kind, option):

        After an action on the same page, only the changed lines are sent when that is much shorter: the model still
        has its latest full view (worker.py keeps it), and unchanged lines keep their refs. Only with `brief` (the
        browser tools, whose result the model gets as is). `fresh` marks a whole view the model now holds (a
        worker's first prompt); other callers (helpers that reshape the text) get it whole and reset the baseline.
        """

        page = self.page
        await self._collect_closed(page)
        self.stamp += 1
        if offset == 0:
            try:

                try:

class Mailbox:
    """The bidder's webmail, worked by the model on request; one request at a time in its tab."""

    def __init__(self, session: SiteSession, briefing: Briefing, deadline: float):
        self.session, self.briefing, self.deadline = session, briefing, deadline
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self.last_tan = ""

    async def address(self) -> str:
        """The bidder's own address, or "" when the webmail cannot tell: never an error that would stop the bid."""
        try:
            async with self.lock:
                found, _ = await run_worker(
                    self.session, "Find the email address of the mailbox you are signed in to (the bidder's own "
                    "address, usually shown as the signed-in account). Return it at once.",
                    MailboxAddress, deadline=self.deadline, max_steps=8, notes=False)
        except Exception as error:
            self.session.trace.event(self.session.name, "stopped", reason=f"address: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
            return ""
        return found.address if found else ""

    async def tan(self, answer: str = "") -> SigningTan | None:
        """
        The signing TAN just requested. The sites run on the scenario's clock, so "newest" is the request's own
        number or reference, else the highest request number or what the mailbox lists as newest, never a
        wall-clock time. `answer` is what the bid website said to the request (it may name the request), so the
        mail worker can pick that very message. A first try with thinking off, a second with thinking on.
        """
        older = f" The TAN {self.last_tan} you returned before is no longer valid." if self.last_tan else ""
        said = (f" The bid website answered the request with: {answer!r}; pick the message for that request."
                if answer else "")
        for thinking in (llm.thinking("tan", False), True):
            try:
                found = await self._tan(tan_goal(self.briefing.tender_reference, said, older), answer, thinking)
            except Exception as error:  # the bid worker asks again; an error here must not stop the bid
                self.session.trace.event(self.session.name, "stopped",
                                         reason=f"tan: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")
                found = None
            if found or self.deadline - time.monotonic() < TAN_RETRY_SECONDS:
                return found
        return None

    async def _tan(self, goal: str, answer: str, thinking: bool) -> SigningTan | None:
        async with self.lock:
            async with self.session.lock:  # the list the tab shows predates the request: load it again
                await self.session.revive()
                await self.session._goto(self.session.page.url)
            found, _ = await run_worker(self.session, goal, SigningTan, context=answer, deadline=self.deadline,
                                        max_steps=TAN_STEPS, notes=False, thinking=thinking)
        if found:
            self.last_tan = found.tan
        return found


TAN_STEPS = 16
TAN_RETRY_SECONDS = 60  # a second TAN lookup only with at least this much time left

            "preview stays empty, open the message's own page. Copy the TAN exactly from its text and return it "

input.prompt:
Web research task (read-only; use web search and page fetches; you may also read files in /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/error404ai_ehl_finals-speed for context, but edit nothing). Goal: find concrete, published techniques for making an LLM-driven web/browser agent finish a multi-site task much faster, and rank which would fit OUR agent. We want total run time down from about 3.5-5.5 minutes to about 90 seconds, at equal answer quality.

Our agent (Python, pydantic-ai, Playwright over CDP to remote browsers, hosted Qwen "flash" model with optional thinking, ~1-4 s per call, 64 concurrent calls allowed, prefix caching automatic):
- Task: read four German business websites (tender portal with Q&A, supplier portal with a spec document in revisions, ERP with materials/prices/stock, webmail with ~9 kinds of approval/authority mails), compute a bid deterministically in Python, enter it in a multi-step server-side form wizard, fetch a TAN from the webmail and sign.
- Measured good run, 229 s: research 0-120 s (parallel workers per site; mail search is the long pole: 9 record kinds, each its own worker loop of 7-14 thinking-on model steps taking 26-87 s, 90 calls total = 39 % of cost; each kept mail is read by its own thinking-on call, 14 calls); ERP: one search worker per catalogue group plus one detail worker per candidate material (22 calls); spec: two parallel attempts. Then the form: 80 s with only 5 model calls (scripted helper fills each position page: a select + "apply" button round trip per cascade level, then save; 5 positions strictly sequential on one tab because the wizard is server-side and per session). Then review + TAN request + mail lookup + submit: 27 s.
- Each worker step = one model call choosing one browser tool (goto/click/fill/select/collect_pages/keep_results...), then the page is re-read as compact text with element refs. Old page views are trimmed from history.
- Hard constraints (competition fair-play rules): a model must choose where to go, what to search and what matters; NOT allowed: a fixed click path, or a crawler/helper that gathers all evidence before model-directed investigation. Allowed helpers: parse a page or document the model chose, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry, fill forms. Several agents and parallel browsers/tabs/contexts are fine. Only the provided browsers may be used (no own browser), but JavaScript run inside a page (e.g. in-page fetch() of same-site URLs the model selected) works. No local models. No hardcoded site knowledge (the final evaluation uses different sites and layouts).

Please research and report on techniques such as (not limited to):
1. Fewer, bigger steps: multi-action/batched tool calls, "plan then execute" or code-generating agents (model writes a short script of actions executed deterministically), parallel tool calling, macro tools.
2. Model-directed bulk reading: the model picks a result list or set of links, a helper fetches/paginates them in parallel (new tabs, or in-page fetch + DOMParser without rendering), then one model call extracts structured records from many documents at once (map-reduce or batched extraction).
3. Observation compaction: accessibility-tree/DOM distillation, diff-only observations, element filtering, so each call is smaller and faster.
4. Speculative/parallel execution: racing or hedging model calls, speculative pre-fetch of likely next pages, starting dependent stages before their inputs are final.
5. Latency engineering for hosted LLMs: streaming with early tool dispatch, prompt-cache-friendly prompt layout, turning reasoning off selectively, smaller output schemas, request hedging.
6. Faster browser mechanics over CDP: avoiding networkidle waits, blocking images/fonts/analytics via routing, reusing contexts, direct form POST via in-page fetch versus clicking through cascading selects, parallel tabs sharing one session.
7. What published fast web agents do (e.g. browser-use "fast agent"/flash mode, Skyvern, Stagehand caching/act replay, Agent-E, WebVoyager follow-ups, OpenAI/Anthropic computer-use guidance, Playwright MCP snapshots, "LLMCompiler" parallel function calling, ReWOO, plan caching/workflow memory such as Agent Workflow Memory). Cite sources with URLs.

For each technique give: what it is (1-2 lines), a source URL, evidence of speed-up if any (numbers), how it would apply to our pipeline (which phase: mail search, mail reading, ERP, spec, form entry, signing), a rough estimate of seconds saved on our 229 s profile, the risk to answer quality or to the fair-play rules above, and implementation effort (S/M/L).

Then give a ranked top 5 for us, and a recommended single "do this first" choice with a short justification, plus what combination could plausibly reach about 90 s total (say so plainly if 90 s looks unrealistic and what the realistic floor is, given ~1-4 s per model call and server round trips of ~0.5-1 s). Keep the final report under about 900 words plus the source list; no long quotes.

Results are in, and the web research you asked for is running in a subagent; I'll pick one approach from it and put it in the plan for your approval, since plan mode is on.

**Public-1 (new `speed-cuts` version), all three at quality 100**

| Run | Quality | Cost | Time | Cost × time |

| `run_681f9e7f9f0bfebe` | 100 | $0.092 | 5:15 | 29.1 |
| `run_82081eadd56df6e3` | 100 | $0.098 | 5:36 | 32.9 |

<result>**Bottom line:** 90 s is a good-run result, not a median. A realistic floor is about 85–100 s, with a median nearer 110–130 s. The largest safe win is in form-entry browser mechanics, not in the model. The seconds-saved figures below are my estimates against your 229 s profile, not measurements.

## What I checked in your repo

- `agent/browser_tools.py:597` waits for `networkidle` (2.5 s timeout) inside `_settle`, in a loop of up to 6. Network-idle needs at least 0.5 s of silence, so every settle pays 0.5–2.5 s.
- `agent/configurator.py` adds fixed sleeps of 0.15–0.3 s per choice (lines 414, 433, 581).
- I did not trace whether every form round trip goes through `_settle`; confirm with one timed run. If it does, 80 s over roughly 25 round trips (about 3.2 s each, against 0.5–1 s of server time) is explained.
- `docs/learned.md` shows you already have multi-action `fill_in`, diff-only views and thinking-off form steps, so those are not listed as new wins.

## Techniques

| # | Technique | Published evidence | Our phase | Est. saved | Risk | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Event-based settle: drop `networkidle`, wait for the navigation response or a DOM change, remove fixed sleeps | Playwright docs call `networkidle` discouraged; one blog measured 0.16 s vs 12.6 s for `goto` (single site) | Form, signing, every worker step | 30–45 s form, 5–10 s elsewhere | None for fair play; stale reads if the wait condition is wrong | S |
| 2 | Plan-then-parallel-execute (LLMCompiler, ReWOO): one call emits all mail queries, a helper runs and paginates them in parallel tabs, a join step picks what to open | LLMCompiler: up to 3.7x latency vs ReAct, 1.35x vs native parallel calls. ReWOO numbers not verified | Mail search (9 loops of 7–14 steps become depth 3–4) | 40–60 s off the mail pole | Medium: the model must pick queries and which mails to open, or it reads as "crawl then one-shot" | M–L |
| 3 | Thinking off on navigation steps, on only for keep/discard judgement; short action outputs | browser-use `flash_mode` skips evaluation, next-goal and thinking; their post: output tokens cost about 215x input per token, 68 s average vs 225–330 s for computer-use models. Your own data: 2–5 s vs 4–27 s | Mail search, ERP search | 20–35 s | Wrong-ref clicks (you saw these); keep a validator | S |
| 4 | Batched extraction over model-chosen documents: helper opens kept mails or ERP detail pages in parallel, one thinking-off call per batch | browser-use `extract` with a separate small model; `page_extraction_llm` | Mail reading (14 calls), ERP details (22 calls) | 5–15 s (already parallel, so mostly tail and cost) | Low; cross-document mix-ups in large batches | S–M |
| 5 | One POST per position: build `FormData` from the live form, set all cascade fields, submit via in-page `fetch`, verify by re-reading, fall back to stepwise | "Beyond Browsing": API-plus-browser hybrid 38.9% vs about 15% browsing-only on WebArena (accuracy, not speed) | Form | 10–20 s beyond #1 | Server may reject skipped cascade states; derived from the DOM, so no hardcoding | M |
| 6 | Within-run workflow memory: the first mail worker posts how search works (box, filters) to the board for the others | AWM: about 2 fewer steps per task, +12 points on WebArena. Cross-run caches (Stagehand, Skyvern "2.3x faster") do not apply: unseen sites, and stored paths count as hardcoding | Mail search, ERP | 8–15 s | Low | S |
| 7 | Hedged model calls: send a duplicate if no first token by about p90, take the first, execute the action once | "Speculative Actions": up to 55% next-action accuracy, up to 20% latency cut. Hedging figures found are library claims only | Long-pole sequential steps | 5–15 s, mainly variance | None for read-only steps; extra cost | S |
| 8 | Speculative staging: open the wizard and fill header and acknowledgement steps during research; pre-open the mailbox before the TAN request | Same paper | Form start, signing | 5–12 s | Rework if inputs change | M |
| 9 | Block images, fonts and analytics | Scraping guides, no solid numbers | All | 2–8 s | Low | S |
| 10 | Cache-friendly prompt order (static prefix, history, then page view) | browser-use post; Alibaba implicit cache from 256 tokens, hits at 20% price, not guaranteed | All | 0–5 s (you are at 40–55% cached) | None | S |

On #9, from my own knowledge rather than a source: Playwright `route()` handlers run in your Python process, so over remote CDP each request costs an extra round trip. The CDP call `Network.setBlockedURLs` blocks inside the browser and avoids that.

## Ranked top 5

1. Event-based settle (#1).
2. Mail plan-then-parallel-execute (#2), with the within-run search recipe (#6).
3. Selective thinking-off for navigation (#3).
4. Single POST per position with fallback (#5).
5. Hedging plus speculative staging (#7, #8).

## Do this first

Start with #1. It is the only large win with no answer-quality or fair-play exposure, and one traced run confirms it. It also speeds every worker step, so research gets shorter as a side effect.

## Can it reach 90 s?

| Phase | Now | With top 5 | What bounds it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Research | 120 s | 40–55 s | Login plus 4–6 sequential model steps at 2–4 s plus page loads; the next pole (ERP or tender Q&A) takes over once mail drops |
| Form | 80 s | 25–35 s (#1), 15–20 s (#1 + #5) | About 25 server round trips at 0.5–1 s, 5 model calls |
| Review and signing | 27 s | 15–20 s | TAN mail arrival and two server steps |
| Total | 229 s | 85–110 s | |

| 1 | Event-based settle on every step (no `networkidle`, no fixed sleeps, one probe instead of the helper sweep) | 35-55 s | low |
| 2 | Mail search as plan-then-parallel-execute (model plans queries, helper runs them in parallel, model picks) | 40-60 s | medium, fair-play care |
| 3 | Thinking off on navigation steps only | 20-35 s | medium (already hurt mail once) |
| 4 | One POST per form position with fallback | 10-20 s | medium |
| 5 | Hedged calls, speculative staging | 5-15 s | low |

-> `_settle` (552): `networkidle` (at least 0.5 s of silence, 2.5 s cap), then `_login`, `_cookies` (two browser

  runs (read-only), so the baseline for the comparison is known and the `err404-layout` zero is explained.

   `tests/test_press.py` for: a page that keeps polling (cap respected), an action that changes the page in place,
   a sign-in page after an action (login helper still runs), a cookie notice (still answered), a short error page
   (still reloaded).
2. Public-1: three `dev/test-run.sh v2 "event settle" event-settle` runs, all 100; compare the new settle totals
   and the form phase against the stage 1a runs.
3. Evals: one `python3 dev/trainloop.py step "event settle"` on the four evals; no `main` baseline rerun (the
   06:45 UTC baseline entries are collected with `adopt`). The synth portal must stay at 100.
4. Record runs in `experiments/runs.jsonl`, add a `docs/learned.md` bullet with the measured seconds.

## Stop points

- Report after verification: quality, cost, time, cost x time, settle seconds saved, eval rewards. Then decide on
  rank 2 (mail plan-then-parallel) together.
- No `atira submit`, no promotion of a test run, no push, without confirmation.

Changes, all in `agent/browser_tools.py` unless noted:

1. **Count requests instead of waiting for `networkidle`.** `_watch(page)` (439) already hooks each page: add
   request / requestfinished / requestfailed counters. `_settle` waits for `domcontentloaded`, then until no
   request has been in flight for about 100 ms, capped at the present 2.5 s.
2. **One probe instead of the helper sweep.** A single in-page `evaluate` returns: a visible password field,
   the texts of visible buttons (max 20), body text length, and whether a human-check widget is present. Python
   applies the existing `COOKIE*` and `ERROR_PAGE` patterns to that result and calls `_login`, `_cookies`,
   `_error_page`, `_human_check` only when the probe says they have work. Helpers themselves stay unchanged.
3. **Replace the fixed sleeps** in `act` (0.25 s) and in `fill_in` (`agent/submit.py:199, 204`) and
   `configurator.py:414, 433, 581` with a wait on the effect (request started, or DOM changed via a
   MutationObserver flag set before the action), with the old sleep as the upper bound.
4. **Measure it.** `settle` records its duration; `tracing.print_summary` prints total and count of settle seconds
   per site, so one test run shows the saving and where time is left.
5. **Off switch** `AGENT_SETTLE=full` restores today's behaviour for A/B and as a fallback.

Not in this step: mail plan-then-parallel (next, rank 2), thinking changes, direct form POST.

## How it gets done

- A general-purpose subagent implements it in `error404ai_ehl_finals-speed` on `speed-cuts`, briefed with this plan,
  the files and line numbers above, the constraint that no site-specific text may enter `agent/`, and the test
  commands below. I review its diff and run the verification myself before reporting.
- Before it starts I read the phase timings of the three finished public runs and the logs of the two 18:32 eval
  runs (read-only), so the baseline for the comparison is known and the `err404-layout` zero is explained.

## Verification

1. `(cd agent && uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests)`: all green, plus new tests beside
   `tests/test_press.py` for: a page that keeps polling (cap respected), an action that changes the page in place,
   a sign-in page after an action (login helper still runs), a cookie notice (still answered), a short error page
   (still reloaded).
2. Public-1: three `dev/test-run.sh v2 "event settle" event-settle` runs, all 100; compare the new settle totals
   and the form phase against the stage 1a runs.
3. Evals: one `python3 dev/trainloop.py step "event settle"` on the four evals; no `main` baseline rerun (the
   06:45 UTC baseline entries are collected with `adopt`). The synth portal must stay at 100.
4. Record runs in `experiments/runs.jsonl`, add a `docs/learned.md` bullet with the measured seconds.

## Stop points

- Report after verification: quality, cost, time, cost x time, settle seconds saved, eval rewards. Then decide on
  rank 2 (mail plan-then-parallel) together.
- No `atira submit`, no promotion of a test run, no push, without confirmation.

input.description: Implement event-based settle
input.prompt:
You are implementing one focused change in a Python web-agent repo. Work ONLY in the git worktree /Users/akshatkhair/Documents/Projects/error404ai_ehl_finals-speed (branch `speed-cuts`). It already has uncommitted changes from me (a `SiteSession.press` method in agent/browser_tools.py, edits in agent/submit.py, agent/configurator.py, agent/llm.py, tests): keep them, build on them, do not revert anything. Do NOT commit, push, run `atira` commands, start sandbox/test/eval runs, or touch files outside this worktree. Do not edit CLAUDE.md, docs/, experiments/ or dev/.

## Background
`agent/` is a pydantic-ai browser agent (Playwright, async) that works several business websites through remote browsers and fills a web form. Read agent/browser_tools.py fully first (class `SiteSession`: `_watch`, `settle`, `_settle_fresh`, `_settle`, `_safely`, `_login`, `_cookies`, `_human_check`, `_error_page`, `_collect_closed`, `look`, `act`, `press`, `_goto`), and skim agent/tracing.py (`Trace`, `print_summary`), agent/submit.py (`fill_in`, `_perform`), agent/configurator.py (`choice_options`, `pick_option`, typeahead branch in `fill_position`).

Today every browser action pays a fixed cost that adds up over ~245 steps per run and ~25 form round trips:
- `SiteSession.act`: `await asyncio.sleep(0.25)` then `self.settle()`.
- `_settle`: `wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 15000)`, then `wait_for_load_state("networkidle", timeout=2500)` (needs >= 0.5 s of network silence), then `_wait_answer`, then the helper sweep `_login`, `_cookies`, `_error_page`, `_human_check`, each one or many round trips to a REMOTE browser (`_cookies` makes two calls per visible button, up to 20 buttons), then `_collect_closed`.
- Fixed sleeps in `fill_in` (agent/submit.py, 0.15 s per action and 0.25 s at the end) and agent/configurator.py (0.3 s after opening a combobox, 0.15 s in `pick_option` for non-select options, 0.3 s typeahead).

## The change: event-based settle on every browser step
Implement these five items. Match the surrounding code style: same comment density (docstrings that explain why, in plain words), line length about 115, naming idiom, no new dependencies.

1. Count requests instead of waiting for `networkidle`. In `_watch(page)` hook `request`, `requestfinished`, `requestfailed` on the page and keep, per page, the number of requests in flight and the monotonic time of the last change (a small dict or attributes keyed by page; clean up when the page closes). In `_settle`, after `domcontentloaded`, wait until no request has been in flight for about 0.1 s, capped at the present 2.5 s. A page that polls forever must still be released at the cap. Long-lived requests (event streams, websockets do not count as requests) must not hold it past the cap.

2. One probe instead of the helper sweep. Add one in-page `evaluate` (guarded by a timeout like the existing probes; module constant JS string next to the other JS constants) that returns: whether a VISIBLE password input exists, the texts/values of visible `button` and `input[type=submit]` elements (max 20, same set `_cookies` looks at), the body's innerText length plus the text itself when it is short (<= 1500 chars, what `_error_page` needs), and whether anything `HUMAN_CHECK_JS` acts on is present (read HUMAN_CHECK_JS to see what it targets; if a cheap presence test is not possible for a part of it, treat that part as "maybe" and still call the helper). Python then applies the EXISTING patterns (`COOKIE`, `COOKIE_ANSWER`, `COOKIE_MINIMAL`, `ERROR_PAGE`) to the probe result and calls `_login`, `_cookies`, `_error_page`, `_human_check` only when the probe says that helper has work. The helpers themselves stay unchanged and keep their behaviour and trace events. Frames: `_human_check` runs per frame today; make sure a human check inside an iframe is still found (probe frames too, or keep calling `_human_check` when the page has child frames). If the probe itself fails or times out, fall back to the full sweep. The outer loop (`for _ in range(6)`: re-settle after a helper acted) stays.

3. Replace the fixed sleeps with a wait on the effect, the old sleep being the upper bound... concretely: in `SiteSession.act`, instead of the unconditional `asyncio.sleep(0.25)` before `settle()`, wait until either a request started or the DOM changed (use the request counter from item 1 and/or a MutationObserver flag installed just before the action), for at most 0.25 s. Do the same for the 0.15/0.25 s sleeps in `fill_in` and the 0.3/0.15/0.3 s sleeps in configurator.py, each capped at its old value. Put the shared wait in ONE small helper (on SiteSession or a module function) and reuse it; configurator.py functions receive `session` or an element, so pick the signature that needs the fewest call-site changes. Where a session-like test double without the new method is passed (agent/tests use fakes, e.g. tests/test_form_shapes.py `Session`, tests/test_signing.py `FakeSession`/`PositionPage`, tests/test_configurator.py), keep things working: update the fakes minimally rather than adding hasattr checks all over the production code.

4. Measure it. `settle` records its duration; keep per-session totals (count and seconds) and have the end-of-run summary print one line per site with settle count and total seconds. Look at how `tracing.print_summary` and `llm.usage_table()` are printed from agent/agent.py and follow that pattern (a module-level registry or a function in browser_tools that agent.py prints). Do not emit a trace event per settle to stdout (too noisy); a quiet/file-only event is fine.

5. Off switch. `AGENT_SETTLE=full` (read once, module constant) restores today's behaviour exactly: `networkidle` wait, the full helper sweep, the fixed sleeps. Default is the new behaviour. `SiteSession.press` (already there) should use the new probe for its "is this a plain page" check where that removes duplication, but keep its semantics: sign-in page, short page, no navigation or any failure -> full settle.

Correctness requirements (do not trade these for speed):
- After a click that navigates, `look()` must never read the OLD page: a navigation that has started must be waited for.
- A sign-in page appearing after an action must still be signed in automatically; a cookie notice still answered with the necessary-only choice; a short transient error page still reloaded; a human check still solved; a hung page still detected (`_wait_answer` path stays).
- Nothing site-specific may be added: no site names, URLs, labels or values from any website; only generic patterns already in the file.

## Tests
Add tests in a new file agent/tests/test_settle.py, in the style of agent/tests/test_press.py (local ThreadingHTTPServer + headless Chromium + a real SiteSession; invented pages, German or English labels are fine but invented). Cover at least: (a) a page that keeps polling in the background is released at the cap and not earlier than its first load; (b) an action that changes the page in place returns the new content; (c) a click that navigates returns the new page, never the old one, also when the server answers after ~0.5 s; (d) a sign-in page after an action gets signed in (credentials come from `site["credentials"]`); (e) a cookie notice is still answered; (f) a short error page (text matching the existing ERROR_PAGE pattern) is still reloaded; (g) with AGENT_SETTLE=full the old path is used (e.g. assert via the module constant or a patched flag); (h) on a plain content page the helper sweep is NOT called (count calls by patching the helpers) while the probe is.

Run, from the worktree:
  cd agent && uv run --no-sync python -m unittest tests.test_settle tests.test_press tests.test_auto_positions tests.test_form_shapes tests.test_configurator tests.test_signing tests.test_bid_flow tests.test_dead_page tests.test_site_tools
then the whole suite once (takes ~4 minutes):
  cd agent && uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests
All must pass. If an existing test fails because of your change, fix the cause; only adjust a test when it encodes the old timing (say so in your report).

Also measure locally, without any network or model: write a tiny throwaway script in your scratch space (not in the repo) or a test that times N=20 `act` clicks on a local page under both modes and report the mean seconds per action for default vs AGENT_SETTLE=full.

## Report back (concise)
- What you changed, per file, with the key function names.
- Test results (counts), and the measured per-action times in both modes.
- Anything you could not make event-based and why, and any behaviour you are unsure about (be specific: which helper, which case).
- Do not claim sandbox or real-site results; you have none.

input.message:
Two measurements from real sandbox runs that change details of the settle work (same worktree, same rules).
1. `SiteSession.press` almost never takes its fast path: its "plain page" test requires body text longer than 1500 characters, and a form step page is often shorter than that, so every form click falls back to the full settle (form phase measured 61-91 s, unchanged). Fix it as part of item 5: a page is NOT plain only when it shows a visible password field, OR its short text actually matches the existing ERROR_PAGE pattern, OR the probe finds cookie-notice buttons or a human check. Length alone must not force the full settle. Update tests/test_press.py accordingly (the "short page" case becomes: a short page WITHOUT an error text takes the fast path; a short page WITH text matching ERROR_PAGE gets the full settle).
2. On one site every page carries a human check (the trace shows `helper action='human_check' done=['unlock slider', 'robot check', ...]` after every single action, and each action costs 2.3-2.9 s there). So the probe's human-check detection is on the hot path: it must be cheap and must never miss one (a missed check leaves the page locked). If HUMAN_CHECK_JS is itself one evaluate per frame that both detects and solves, it is fine to keep calling it directly instead of probing for it first; just make sure the request-idle wait and the rest of the sweep do not add fixed time around it, and that after a solved check the loop re-settles as today. Add a test with an invented locked page that the existing HUMAN_CHECK_JS can solve (read the JS to see what it looks for), asserting it is still solved in the default mode and reporting the per-action time.
Report the same things as before, plus the measured per-action time on the human-check page in both modes.

content.text:
Two things came out of the logs, and one of them is a problem with my stage 1a changes that I need to pin down before going further.

**Why the public runs weren't faster**
- **Form phase: 91 s, 61 s and 81 s**, against about 80 s before. The quick-click helper almost never took its fast path: it treated any page with less than 1,500 characters of text as suspicious and fell back to the slow wait, and form step pages are short. I've passed that fix to the subagent.
- **Research ended at 184–248 s**, against 120 s in the best `main` run. That variance, not the form, decided the totals.
- **TAN lookup failed on the first try in 2 of 3 runs**, costing about 60 s each: the mail worker used all 16 of its steps without returning the TAN, and the second attempt found it in 15 s.
- **Mail pages cost 2.3–2.9 s per action** because every page carries a slider and "not a robot" check. That confirms the settle work is aimed at the right place.

**The eval zeros are not from the platform outage**

| Eval | `main` | New version | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Synth portal | 0 | 100 | Save-click fix |
| `err404-traps` | 100 | 100 | No change |
| `err404-layout` | 46.9 | 0 | Bid never signed |
| `err404-nobid` | 0 | 0 | Bid never signed in the new version |

On `err404-layout` the new version filled the form and reached the signing step at 5:24, then the TAN lookup failed 13 times in a row until the deadline. `main` on the same eval also failed the lookup twice before succeeding on the third try, so the lookup is fragile there to begin with. Thirteen straight failures is unlikely to be chance though, so I'm treating it as possibly caused by my changes (the mail-tab warm-up or the changed signing step are the candidates) until I've seen what the mail browser was showing. I've requested the screen recording at that moment; the platform is slow to return it.

So the honest state of stage 1a: it fixed your portal and held 100 on public-1, but it did not speed anything up yet, and it may have made TAN lookup worse. I won't run anything new on the platform until the lookup question is answered and the subagent's settle work is reviewed.

Here is where things stand while the combined candidate's runs finish.

**Found and fixed: why the layout eval scored 0**
- That site calls the TAN a "signing code". A search for "TAN" returns nothing, and the lookup worker saw the right mail in the list without recognising it. `main` has the same weakness there; it failed twice before a lucky third try.
- Two general fixes: the lookup now judges a message by what it is for, not by the word, and it is told what the bid site said about the request (that text was being dropped because it contained a link).
- Verified locally on the layout eval: the lookup found "Signing code 1" in 7 seconds and the bid was signed and accepted. That local run still scored only 5, because its research built no positions; that is a separate problem from signing.

So the earlier worry that my stage 1a changes broke TAN lookup is cleared: it was an existing weakness.

**The combined candidate now running**
A helper answering your side questions built it from a teammate's build #114 (batched mail research, cheaper) plus my fixes: the save click, the quick form click, the warm mail tab, TAN entry and submit in one step, and the TAN wording.

- 3 public-1 test runs: `run_4390931aaa48bc4b`, `run_259408efb54d003b`, `run_a130d3ec7fbeb109`.
- 4 eval runs, labelled `combo-20261011-0937-CEST` on https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/evals.

One thing to know about it: the candidate sits in a temporary folder, not on a git branch, so it isn't reproducible from the repo yet. If the results are good, it needs to be put on a branch properly before anyone submits it.

**Still open**
- The subagent's event-based settle change is still in progress and is not part of this candidate.
- I'll post the public and eval results for the combined candidate as soon as they finish.

The combined candidate's results are complete, the event-based settle change is finished but unverified on the platform, and a slimmer final candidate is running now.

**Combined candidate (teammate build #114 plus all my changes)**

| Where | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Public-1, 3 runs | 100, 100, 100 at $0.059–0.076 and 3:50–6:39; cost × time 13.5, 28.4, 29.1 |
| Your synth portal | 100 (`main`: 0) |
| `err404-traps` | 100, in 5:34 for $0.083 (`main`: 100 in about 12 min for more than twice that) |
| `err404-layout` | 51.3 (`main`: 46.9; my earlier version: 0) |
| `err404-nobid` | 0 (`main`: 0) |

So it holds 100 on public-1, costs about a third less than `main`, and is at or above `main` on every eval. `err404-nobid` is still 0 for every version; nothing so far handles that case.

**What its logs showed about my speed changes**
The helper that built it read the run logs and found my speed-ups weren't paying off, so it cut them:
- The form phase took 90 s and 121 s with my changes, against 28–82 s for the teammate build alone.
- Three of my six public runs needed two or three TAN lookups, losing 60–120 s each, while the teammate build found the TAN first time in all five of its runs. The mail-tab warm-up reload is the suspect; that isn't proven.

**Final candidate, running now** (label `final-20261011-0947-CEST`)
Teammate build #114 with only the two fixes that are proven: the save click that can't end the run, and the TAN lookup that recognises a differently named signing code. Three public-1 runs and four eval runs are in progress, about 4 minutes in.

**Event-based settle (the subagent's work)**
It's implemented in the `speed-cuts` worktree and the full suite passes locally (409 tests, 25 new). Locally it cuts the wait per browser action from 0.28–0.96 s to 0.09–0.22 s. It has not run on the platform and is in neither candidate. The subagent flagged one real risk: a page that starts its request slightly after a click could be read too early.

**Expectation for the final candidate:** cost × time around 11–17, which is 4th or 5th on the public board, not 3rd. Its edge over build #114 is on unfamiliar sites.

I'll post the final candidate's numbers when its runs finish. Neither candidate is on a git branch yet; both are in a temporary folder and need to be put in the repo before anyone submits.

Pushed, and the next speed step is now running on the platform.

**Pushed: branch `form-save-click`** (one commit on top of the latest `main`, `e1d0854`)
- The form's save click falls back to a scripted click and can no longer end the run. This is the fix that took your synth portal from 0 to 100.
- The TAN lookup is told what the bid site said about the request even when that sentence contains a link.
- I left out the TAN wording change, because a teammate had already put an equivalent fix on `main`.
- 30 form and signing tests pass, including a new one for a covered save button. The commit follows the team convention (author `josteng`, no trailers). It is a branch only; nothing is merged or submitted.

**Final candidate's eval results are complete: 100 on all four**

| Eval | `main` | Final candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your synth portal | 0 | 100 |
| `err404-traps` | 100 | 100 |
| `err404-layout` | 46.9 | 100 |
| `err404-nobid` | 0 | 100 |

That is one run per eval, and the earlier combined candidate scored 0 on `err404-nobid`, so treat the no-bid result as unconfirmed until it repeats. That candidate is a teammate's unpushed build plus these fixes, which is why it isn't what I pushed; I can only push what is ours.

**Running now: the event-based settle version** (local branch `event-settle`, not pushed)
- It is the latest `main` plus the pushed fixes, the subagent's settle work and the quick form click. I removed the mail warm-up and the one-step TAN entry, since the run logs counted against them.
- All 429 agent tests pass on it.
- 3 public-1 test runs (`run_bfcea78955105b20`, `run_bcc075b06b3a89d8`, `run_199ad099e1b5a40b`) and 4 eval runs labelled `settle-20261011-1007-CEST`.

**On 1.5 minutes:** this step should take seconds off every browser action, but it will not reach 90 s alone. The other large piece is the batched mail research in your teammate's build #114; once that is on `main`, the two together are the realistic route. I'll report the measured times and the per-site settle totals when these runs finish.
